catalog.name: Accounts Receivable calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the accounts receivable domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the rounding and sign conventions, the dynamic synchronisation of the derived line families, the due date algorithm in its four delay types, the payment term amount distribution with its balance rule and its cash rounding correction, the early payment discount in its three computation modes and the write-off computed at payment time, the discount allocation lines, cash rounding under both strategies and all three coin methods, the document totals and their signed variants, the numbering of documents with its scope, its starting numbers and its accounting date corrections, the six payment reference generators with the modulo arithmetic of the structured creditor reference, the instalment and portal payment computations, the foreign-currency rules with the exchange difference on settlement, and the miscellaneous computed quantities.
catalog.authored_from: docs/domains/accounts-receivable/calculations.md, with the ledger effects of docs/domains/accounts-receivable/accounting-effects.md, the days-sales-outstanding of docs/domains/accounts-receivable/entities.md and the rule identifiers of docs/domains/accounts-receivable/business-rules.md

records.name: Rounding a monetary amount to the precision of a currency
records.purpose: Reduces any intermediate monetary result of the domain to a value the currency can represent, so that every amount stored on a document or on one of its journal items sits on the smallest increment of the currency it is expressed in.

operands.name: value to round
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency it is rounded to
operands.source: the intermediate result of any monetary computation of the domain
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: target currency
operands.source: the document currency when no currency is named, the company currency for a balance, the line currency for an amount in currency
operands.constraints: must be known before the amount can be stored

operands.name: rounding step of the target currency
operands.source: the rounding step recorded on the currency, for example 0.01 for a currency with two decimal places
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: The currency to round to is known; where the document names none, the document currency is meant.
preconditions.otherwise: The amount cannot be stored and the computation that produced it is not meaningful.

preconditions.condition: The rounding step of that currency is strictly greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The value is left unchanged.

procedure: Take the value produced by the computation and the currency it belongs to.
Round the value to the number of decimal places of that currency, resolving a tie away from zero, on the currency's rounding step.
Return the rounded value; the full arithmetic of the rounding primitive belongs to the multi-currency documents of this repository.
records.formula: round( x , C ) = the value x rounded to the number of decimal places of currency C, half away from zero on the rounding step of C

rounding.what: Every monetary quantity of the domain at the moment it is stored or compared.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the target currency, derived from that currency's rounding step.
rounding.step: At the end of each monetary computation, before the value is written to a document or to a journal item.

result.name: rounded amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the amount field it was computed for, and displayed with the number of decimal places of that currency.

edge_cases.case: The value lies exactly on a half unit of the last decimal place, for example 362.205 on a two-decimal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The half is carried away from zero, giving 362.21.

edge_cases.case: The value is negative and lies exactly on a half unit, for example minus 362.205.
edge_cases.outcome: The half is carried away from zero, giving minus 362.21.

edge_cases.case: No currency is named in the expression.
edge_cases.outcome: The document currency is used.

edge_cases.case: The value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero and the sign is immaterial.

worked_examples.description: Thirty per cent of a gross total on a two-decimal currency.
worked_examples.narrative: Thirty per cent of 1 207.35 is 362.205; the currency carries two decimal places, so the half is carried away from zero and the stored amount is 362.21.

worked_examples.description: A tax amount that needs no adjustment.
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-one per cent of a base of 82.69 is 17.3649, which rounds down to 17.36 because the third decimal is below five.

records.name: The zero test at the precision of a currency
records.purpose: Decides whether a computed amount counts as nothing, so that a derived journal item whose amount vanishes at the currency's precision is not created and a correction that vanishes is not applied.

operands.name: value to test
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency it is tested against
operands.source: a cash rounding difference, an instalment correction, a discount amount or the amount of a candidate derived line
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: target currency
operands.source: the document currency, unless the expression names another
operands.constraints: must be known

preconditions.condition: The currency the value is tested against is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The document currency is used.

procedure: Round the value to the precision of the target currency by the rounding convention of this catalogue.
Compare the rounded value with zero.
Report true when the rounded value equals zero and false otherwise.
records.formula: is_zero( x , C ) = true when round( x , C ) = 0, and false otherwise

rounding.what: The value being tested, before the comparison.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the target currency.
rounding.step: Immediately before the comparison with zero; the comparison itself never rounds again.

result.name: zero indication
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the routine that asked the question.

edge_cases.case: The value is 0.004 on a two-decimal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to 0.00, so the test reports true and the amount counts as nothing.

edge_cases.case: The value is 0.005 on a two-decimal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to 0.01, so the test reports false and the amount counts as something.

edge_cases.case: The value is minus 0.004 on a two-decimal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to 0.00 and the test reports true.

edge_cases.case: The currency has no decimal places and the value is 0.4.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to 0 and the test reports true.

worked_examples.description: A cash rounding difference that vanishes.

expected_outputs.consequence: no correction is applied to the instalment and no cash rounding line is created

worked_examples.narrative: A gross total that is already a multiple of the coin gives a difference of 0.00, the test reports true, and the recomputation of the cash rounding line deletes any existing line and stops.

worked_examples.description: A cash rounding difference of two hundredths.

expected_outputs.consequence: the cash rounding line is created with a balance of minus 0.02

worked_examples.narrative: Minus 0.02 rounds to minus 0.02, the test reports false, and the difference is written onto a rounding line.

records.name: Converting an amount between the document currency and the company currency at the document rate
records.purpose: Gives every journal item of a foreign-currency document its company-currency balance from the amount stated in the document currency, and the reverse, so that the two currency columns of the entry stay consistent.

operands.name: amount in document currency
operands.source: the amount in currency of a journal item, or a total of the document
operands.constraints: carries the accounting sign

operands.name: currency rate of the document
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate stored on the document
operands.constraints: strictly positive; a non-positive rate is refused

operands.name: company currency
operands.source: the currency of the company that owns the document
operands.constraints: the balance is always expressed in it

preconditions.condition: The document carries a strictly positive currency rate.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message “The currency rate must be strictly positive.”

preconditions.condition: The document currency differs from the company currency for the conversion to have any effect.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one and the two amounts are equal.

procedure: Divide the amount stated in the document currency by the document's currency rate.
Round the quotient to the company currency.
For the opposite direction, multiply the amount known in company currency by the rate and round to the document currency.
records.formula: amount_in_company_currency = round( amount_in_document_currency ÷ rate , company_currency )   and   amount_in_document_currency = round( amount_in_company_currency × rate , document_currency )

rounding.what: The converted amount.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the currency the amount is converted into.
rounding.step: After the division or the multiplication, once, before the amount is stored.

result.name: converted amount
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency in the first direction, the document currency in the second
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the balance of the journal item in the first direction, as the amount in currency in the second.

edge_cases.case: The document currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one, no conversion is performed and both amounts are equal.

edge_cases.case: The rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The routines that divide by the rate produce zero instead of dividing; the constraint on a strictly positive rate prevents a zero rate on an invoice whose currency differs from the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The amount in document currency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The converted amount is zero in both directions.

edge_cases.case: The rate is edited after the lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax synchronisation switches to the source that reapplies the currency rate: the amounts in currency of the tax lines are preserved and only their balances are recomputed.

worked_examples.description: A net amount of one thousand dollars on a document whose rate is 1.0850 dollars for one euro.
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand divided by 1.0850 is 921.658986 and more, which rounds to 921.66 in the company currency.

worked_examples.description: The tax of the same document.
worked_examples.narrative: Two hundred and ten divided by 1.0850 is 193.548387 and more, which rounds to 193.55.

records.name: The direction sign of a document
records.purpose: Converts between the amounts a customer reads on the printed document, which are always positive, and the accounting amounts stored on the journal items, where a debit is positive and a credit is negative.

operands.name: document type
operands.source: the type field of the document
operands.constraints: one of customer invoice, customer credit note, sales receipt, vendor bill, vendor credit note, purchase receipt or plain entry

preconditions.condition: The document has a type.
preconditions.otherwise: The document is treated as a plain entry and the sign is plus one.

procedure: Read the document type.
Return plus one for an outbound document, which is a customer credit note, a vendor bill or a purchase receipt, and for a plain entry.
Return minus one for an inbound document, which is a customer invoice, a sales receipt or a vendor credit note.
records.formula: sign = +1 for a customer credit note, a vendor bill, a purchase receipt or a plain entry ; sign = −1 for a customer invoice, a sales receipt or a vendor credit note

rounding.what: Nothing; the sign is exactly plus one or minus one.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: direction sign
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; it multiplies the amounts of every product line, tax line and total of the document.

edge_cases.case: The document is a plain journal entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is plus one and the customer-facing figures coincide with the accounting figures.

edge_cases.case: A product line of a customer invoice carries a negative quantity times unit price.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is flagged as a reversal line for the purposes of the debit and credit columns, but the direction sign of the document is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The distribution of the payment term amounts is asked for its own sign parameter.
edge_cases.outcome: For a stored document that parameter is plus one when the document is inbound and minus one otherwise, which is the opposite of the direction sign.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with a product line of one thousand.
worked_examples.narrative: The tax engine returns a positive tax-excluded total of 1 000.00; multiplied by the direction sign of minus one the stored amount is minus 1 000.00, that is a credit of 1 000.00 on the revenue account.

worked_examples.description: A customer credit note with the same line.
worked_examples.narrative: The direction sign is plus one, the stored amount is plus 1 000.00, and the revenue account is debited.

records.name: The reference date of a document for every date-driven computation
records.purpose: Fixes the single date from which the due date of every payment term line, the early payment discount deadline and the payment term preview are counted, so that all of them move together when the document is redated.

operands.name: document date
operands.source: the document date field of the document
operands.constraints: may be empty on a draft

operands.name: accounting date
operands.source: the accounting date field of the document
operands.constraints: may be empty on a draft

operands.name: today
operands.source: the current date of the session
operands.constraints: always available

preconditions.condition: At least one of the three dates is available.
preconditions.otherwise: Today is always available, so the reference date is always defined.

procedure: Take the document date when it is set.
Otherwise take the accounting date when it is set.
Otherwise take today.
records.formula: reference_date = document_date, else accounting_date, else today

rounding.what: Nothing; the reference date is a whole calendar date.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: reference date
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the due date algorithm, the early payment discount deadline and the payment term preview.

edge_cases.case: A draft with neither a document date nor an accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is used, so the due dates move every day until a date is set.

edge_cases.case: The document date is later than the accounting date.
edge_cases.outcome: The document date wins; the accounting date is only a fallback.

edge_cases.case: The document is redated after the payment term lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The needed terms are recomputed and the maturity dates move with the new reference date.

worked_examples.description: An invoice dated the twentieth of January of the year 2026 with an accounting date of the thirty-first of January.
worked_examples.narrative: The document date is set, so it is the reference date and the accounting date is ignored.

worked_examples.description: A draft with no dates at all, edited on the fifth of February of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: Neither date is set, so today is taken.

records.name: The order of the synchronisation stack and the resulting reconciliation order
records.purpose: Fixes the order in which the derived line families of a draft document are recomputed after a write, so that every family sees the final state of the families it depends on and the payment term lines see the final totals.

operands.name: sequence number of each synchroniser
operands.source: the fixed table of the eight synchronisers: payment term lines 10, automatic balancing line 20, cash rounding line 30, discount allocation lines 40, tax lines 50, non-deductible base lines 60, early payment discount lines 70, partner propagation 80
operands.constraints: distinct and fixed

operands.name: document status
operands.source: the status field of the document
operands.constraints: the whole stack is skipped unless the status is draft

preconditions.condition: The document status is draft.
preconditions.otherwise: Every synchroniser skips the document and no derived line is touched.

preconditions.condition: The stack is not already active for this document.
preconditions.otherwise: The recursion guard performs the write and returns without re-entering the stack.

preconditions.condition: The caller has not suppressed the stack.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is performed verbatim, as when the lines of a plain journal entry are copied and negated for a reversal.

procedure: Enter the synchronisers in ascending order of sequence number, each taking its snapshot as it is entered: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, then 80.
Perform the write in the innermost scope.
Reconcile the families in the reverse order of entry, so 80 first and 10 last.

Reconcile the partner propagation first, then the early payment discount lines, the non-deductible base lines, the tax lines, the discount allocation lines, the cash rounding line, the automatic balancing line, and the payment term lines last.
records.formula: entry order = 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80   and   reconciliation order = 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the ordering itself.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: reconciliation order
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, an ordered list of eight synchronisers
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it governs the sequence of the recomputations after every write.

edge_cases.case: A synchroniser's own writes would re-enter the stack.
edge_cases.outcome: The recursion guard skips the re-entry, which is what makes the fixed point reachable in a single pass.

edge_cases.case: The document is a plain journal entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the automatic balancing line synchroniser and the tax line synchroniser apply; the six invoice-only synchronisers do nothing.

edge_cases.case: The document is a sale document.
edge_cases.outcome: The non-deductible synchroniser is entered but produces nothing, because non-deductibility is effective on purchase documents.

worked_examples.description: Raising the quantity on one product line of a draft customer invoice.

inputs.field written: the quantity of one product line

worked_examples.narrative: The eight synchronisers are entered in ascending sequence, the quantity is written, and the families are reconciled in descending sequence, so that the payment term lines are rebuilt from totals that already include the new taxes, the new cash rounding line and the new early payment discount lines.

records.name: The generic reconciliation algorithm for a keyed line family
records.purpose: Brings the lines of one derived family into agreement with what the document needs, creating, updating, deleting or recycling lines, while never destroying a value the user typed by hand.

operands.name: existing keys before the write
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a mapping from line to key
operands.source: every line of the document whose key field of the family is non-empty
operands.constraints: a line with an empty key is not tracked, except an early payment discount line, which is tracked under a synthetic key made of its own identifier

operands.name: needed map before the write
operands.unit_or_currency: amounts in the document currency and in the company currency, per key
operands.source: the aggregation of the needed maps of all contributing records
operands.constraints: aggregated by the rule of the aggregation record of this catalogue

operands.name: existing keys after the write
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a mapping from line to key
operands.source: the same reading, repeated after the write
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: needed map after the write
operands.unit_or_currency: amounts in the document currency and in the company currency, per key
operands.source: the same aggregation, repeated after the write
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: dirty records
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of records
operands.source: the records whose dirty flag of the family is set
operands.constraints: the flag is cleared when the snapshot is taken and recollected after the write

preconditions.condition: At least one contributing record is dirty after the write.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing in the family can have changed and the algorithm stops.

preconditions.condition: The needed map after the write differs from the needed map before the write.
preconditions.otherwise: The algorithm stops, because any difference in the lines is then a deliberate edit by the user and must be preserved.

preconditions.condition: Either the needed map before the write was not empty, or the set of non-trivial existing keys is unchanged.
preconditions.otherwise: The algorithm stops, because the caller created the derived lines itself and the synchroniser must not fight it; a non-trivial key is one that does not merely name a line identifier.

procedure: Before the write, record the mapping from every line with a non-empty key to that key, aggregate the needed maps of the contributing records, collect the dirty records and clear their flags.
Perform the write.
Recollect the dirty records and stop when none is dirty.
Rebuild the existing mapping and the needed map after the write.
Drop from the needed map before the write every key that names a line identifier that no longer exists, so that a line the user deleted is not resurrected.
Build the translation from the old key to the new key for every line present both before and after.
Stop when the needed map after the write equals the needed map before the write.
Stop when the needed map before the write was empty and the set of non-trivial existing keys changed.
Group the existing lines after the write by key, since several lines may share one key.

Compute the deletions: every line that existed before whose old key is absent from the needed map after the write, whose old key is still present in the grouping and whose translated new key is also absent from that needed map, plus every line existing after whose key is absent from that needed map and that is not already listed.
Compute the creations: every key of the needed map after the write that has no line in the grouping.
Compute the updates: every line of every key of the needed map after the write at least one of whose values differs from the needed value.

Recycle: while both a deletion and a creation remain, take one of each and rewrite the line to be deleted with the key, the values and the display type of the line to be created, so that the line identifier survives a change of maturity date or of account.
Delete whatever remains in the deletion list, with the guard against automatic deletion bypassed.
Create whatever remains in the creation list, in a cleaned context so that no stray default reaches the new lines.
Apply the updates.
records.formula: deletions = ( lines before whose old key ∉ needed_after and whose translated key ∉ needed_after ) + ( lines after whose key ∉ needed_after ) ; creations = keys of needed_after with no line ; recycled = min( count of deletions , count of creations ) ; net created = count of creations − recycled ; net deleted = count of deletions − recycled

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the reconciliation itself; the amounts it writes were rounded by the routine that produced the needed map.
rounding.precision: The precision of the currency of each amount in the needed value.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier by the producing routine.
rounding.step: Before the comparison, every value of the needed map is converted to the representation the storage layer would give it, so that a comparison against a stored line never fails on a representation-only difference.

result.name: the reconciled line set of the family
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of journal items
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the lines of the document carrying the family's display type.

edge_cases.case: The needed map after the write is empty and lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: Every line of the family is deleted.

edge_cases.case: One key disappears and another appears in the same write.
edge_cases.outcome: The two are paired by the recycling step and the line identifier is preserved, which matters because other records point at that line.

edge_cases.case: An early payment discount line whose key becomes empty because the payment term no longer carries a discount in the mode that books it on the invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still tracked, under a synthetic key made of its own identifier, so that it is cleaned up rather than orphaned.

edge_cases.case: The user deleted a derived line by hand and nothing else changed.
edge_cases.outcome: The needed maps are equal, the algorithm stops at that test and the line is not recreated.

worked_examples.description: A payment term is changed from a single immediate line to two lines of thirty and seventy per cent on a draft invoice that already carries one receivable line.
worked_examples.narrative: The old key, carrying the single maturity date, is absent from the new needed map, so the existing line is listed for deletion; the two new maturity dates are listed for creation. The recycling step pairs the deletion with the first creation and rewrites the existing line, so one line keeps its identifier and only one line is genuinely created.

worked_examples.description: The same invoice is written again with no change to the payment term.

expected_outputs.stopped at: the test on the dirty records

worked_examples.narrative: No contributing record is dirty, so the algorithm stops immediately and no line is touched.

records.name: Aggregating the needed maps of several contributing records
records.purpose: Merges the needed maps that several product lines produce for the same derived line into one map, so that two lines that need the same discount allocation line or the same early payment discount grouping contribute to a single journal item.

operands.name: contributing needed maps
operands.unit_or_currency: amounts in the document currency and in the company currency, per key
operands.source: the needed map field of every contributing record, one per product line
operands.constraints: a map that is the marker meaning the value was invalidated is skipped

operands.name: monetary fields of a needed value
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
operands.source: the value stored under each key
operands.constraints: only monetary fields are added; the other fields are copied from the first contribution

preconditions.condition: At least one contributing map is present and not the invalidated marker.
preconditions.otherwise: The aggregated map is empty and the family produces no line.

procedure: Start from an empty result.
Take each contributing map in turn, and each key and value pair inside it.
Copy the value when the key is new to the result.
Otherwise add every monetary field of the value into the accumulated value, and remember whether any accumulated monetary field ended up different from zero.
Drop the key entirely when every accumulated monetary field ended at zero, so that a derived line whose amounts cancel is never created.
Skip a contributing map that is the invalidated marker, because the write that invalidated it has scheduled a recomputation.
Convert every value to the representation the storage layer would give it, so that the later comparison against a stored line cannot fail on representation alone.
records.formula: aggregated_value( key ) = Σ over contributing maps of ( monetary fields of value( key ) ) ; the key is dropped when every aggregated monetary field = 0

rounding.what: The accumulated monetary fields.
rounding.precision: The precision of the currency of each field, the document currency for an amount in currency and the company currency for a balance.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, as applied by the routine that produced each contribution.
rounding.step: The addition itself does not round; the final conversion to the storage representation is applied once, after all contributions have been added.

result.name: aggregated needed map
result.unit_or_currency: amounts in the document currency and in the company currency, per key
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the generic reconciliation algorithm.

edge_cases.case: Two contributions to the same key carry opposite amounts.
edge_cases.outcome: Every accumulated monetary field is zero and the key is dropped, so no line is produced.

edge_cases.case: A contributing map is the invalidated marker.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped; the recomputation scheduled by the write that invalidated it will supply the value.

edge_cases.case: Two contributions carry the same key but different non-monetary values, for example a different label.
edge_cases.outcome: The value of the first contribution is kept and only the monetary fields are added.

edge_cases.case: No contributing record produces anything.
edge_cases.outcome: The aggregated map is empty and the reconciliation deletes every line of the family.

worked_examples.description: Two product lines that both need the discount allocation line on the revenue account, one contributing minus 100.00 and the other minus 200.00.
worked_examples.narrative: Both contributions share the key made of the revenue account, the document and the rate, so their monetary fields are added and a single line of minus 300.00 is needed.

worked_examples.description: Two product lines whose contributions to one key cancel.
worked_examples.narrative: Every accumulated monetary field ends at zero, so the key is dropped and no derived line is created.

records.name: The complete synchronisation pass on one write
records.purpose: States the whole ordered algorithm that runs on every write to a draft document or to any of its lines, so that a rebuild reproduces the same derived lines from the same edit.

operands.name: the fields being written
operands.source: the caller's write on the document or on its lines
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: document status
operands.constraints: steps two to eleven are skipped unless the status is draft

operands.name: commercial entity of the document
operands.constraints: propagated to every line when it changes

preconditions.condition: A document exists, possibly not yet stored.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to synchronise.

preconditions.condition: The document status is draft.
preconditions.otherwise: The snapshots and the reconciliations are skipped and only the write is performed.

preconditions.condition: The recursion guard is not already active for this document.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is performed and the routine returns without re-entering the stack.

procedure: Enter the recursion guard; when the stack is already active for this document, perform the write and return.
Snapshot the payment term family: the existing payment term keys, the document's needed terms, and clear the flag that marks the needed terms as dirty.
Snapshot the automatic balancing line on a plain entry: whether the entry currently carries any tax.
Snapshot the cash rounding line: nothing is recorded, because the routine recomputes from scratch afterwards.
Snapshot the discount allocation family: the existing keys, the needed maps of the product lines, and clear their dirty flags.

Snapshot the tax family: per document the currency, the partner, the document type, the currency rate and the document date; per base line, whose display type is `product`, `epd`, `rounding` or `non_deductible_product`, the grouping-key fields plus, on an invoice, the unit price, the quantity, the discount and the deductibility, and on a document that is not an invoice the amount in currency instead; per tax line the amount in currency, the balance and the analytic distribution.
Snapshot the non-deductible family: a multiset over the product lines of the label, the subtotal, the taxes, the deductibility and the account.
Snapshot the early payment discount family: the existing keys, the needed maps of the product lines, and clear their dirty flags.
Snapshot the partner propagation: the commercial entity of the document.
Snapshot the line-level synchronisation, the inner scope that keeps a line's own derived values such as its currency and its label consistent with the document.
Perform the write.
Reconcile the partner: when the commercial entity changed, write it onto every line of the document.

Reconcile the early payment discount lines by the generic reconciliation algorithm, with the needed map computed by the routine that produces the early payment discount lines of the mode that books them on the invoice.
Reconcile the non-deductible lines, on purchase documents only.
Reconcile the tax lines by the detailed tax reconciliation.
Reconcile the discount allocation lines by the generic reconciliation algorithm, with the needed map computed by the discount allocation routine.
Recompute the cash rounding line.

Reconcile the automatic balancing line on a plain entry: when the entry carries taxes before or after the write, create or update a line labelled “Automatic Balancing Line” on the journal's default account, or, absent one, on the company's journal suspense account, so that the entry balances; when the taxes were removed entirely, delete every tax line and clear every tax grid first.
Reconcile the payment term lines by the generic reconciliation algorithm, with the document's needed terms as the needed map.
records.formula: snapshots taken = 9 (payment term, automatic balancing line, cash rounding, discount allocation, tax, non-deductible, early payment discount, partner, line-level) ; reconciliations performed after the write = 8, in the order 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10

rounding.what: Each family rounds its own amounts; the pass itself rounds nothing.
rounding.precision: The document currency for an amount in currency, the company currency for a balance.
rounding.step: Inside each family's own routine, before its needed values are compared with the stored lines.

result.name: the synchronised document
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a document with all its derived lines
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored: every derived line family agrees with its need, the sum of the balances of all lines is zero, and no line the user typed has been silently changed.

edge_cases.case: The document is not yet stored, so its lines have no database identifiers.
edge_cases.outcome: The early payment discount lines and the non-deductible lines do not exist as records, and equivalent base lines are synthesised from the needed maps of the product lines when the tax engine is called.

edge_cases.case: The document status is not draft.
edge_cases.outcome: Every synchroniser skips it; a posted document is never synchronised.

edge_cases.case: The caller suppresses the stack, as when a plain journal entry is reversed and its lines are copied verbatim and negated.
edge_cases.outcome: No snapshot is taken and no family is reconciled.

edge_cases.case: A synchroniser's own writes would re-enter the stack.
edge_cases.outcome: The recursion guard skips the re-entry, so the fixed point is reached in one pass.

worked_examples.description: A draft customer invoice in the company currency with one product line of one thousand at twenty-one per cent, a payment term of a single immediate line, no cash rounding and no discount allocation account; the user raises the quantity from one to two.
worked_examples.narrative: The nine snapshots are taken, the quantity is written, the partner needs no propagation, no early payment discount and no discount allocation line exist, the tax family recomputes the tax line to minus 420.00 from a base of minus 2 000.00, no cash rounding applies, and the payment term family is reconciled last and rebuilds the single receivable line at 2 420.00, so the three balances add to zero.

records.name: The rounding source decision for the tax line reconciliation
records.purpose: Decides whether the tax amounts already stored on a draft document are authoritative or must be recomputed from the bases, which is what preserves a tax amount the user typed by hand while still following a change of price, quantity, currency or rate.

operands.name: document type change
operands.source: the snapshot of the tax family compared with the state after the write
operands.constraints: tested only on an invoice

operands.name: currency change
operands.constraints: tested only on an invoice

operands.name: removal of a base line that carried taxes
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: change of at least one base line
operands.source: the same comparison over the grouping-key fields, the unit price, the quantity, the discount and the deductibility
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: change of the tax line set or protection of a tax line field from recomputation
operands.source: the same comparison; the protection is how a manually typed tax amount is marked
operands.constraints: none

operands.name: currency rate change
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate recorded in the snapshot compared with the rate after the write
operands.constraints: considered only when no earlier condition matched

preconditions.condition: The document status is draft.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax lines are not reconciled at all.

preconditions.condition: The document is an invoice, or a document whose lines carry taxes or tax repartitions.
preconditions.otherwise: The tax synchroniser does not apply.

procedure: Take the first matching condition of the cascade and stop there.
When the document is an invoice and its currency or its document type changed, recompute the tax amounts from the bases.
When a base line that carried taxes was removed, keep the tax amounts only if some tax line value also changed.

When at least one base line changed, keep the tax amounts when either none of the changed lines has taxes now or had taxes before, or the tax line set itself changed, or some tax line field is currently protected from recomputation; and, when the amounts were to be kept and any changed line carries an explicit amount in currency or balance, stop altogether, because the caller supplied everything.
When only the currency rate changed, use the source that reapplies the currency rate: keep the tax amounts in the document currency and recompute only their company-currency counterparts.
When none of the conditions matched, stop; there is nothing to do.
records.formula: rounding_source = recompute from the bases, when the document is an invoice and ( currency changed or document type changed ) ; else keep the tax amounts only if a tax line value changed, when a base line carrying taxes was removed ; else keep the tax amounts when ( no changed line has or had taxes ) or ( the tax line set changed ) or ( a tax line field is protected ), and stop when the amounts would be kept and a changed line carries an explicit amount ; else reapply the currency rate, when the rate changed ; else stop

rounding.what: Under the source that reapplies the currency rate, each tax line's balance.
rounding.precision: The company currency.
rounding.step: Before the tax engine is called: the balance is replaced by the amount in currency divided by the new rate, rounded to the company currency, while the amount in currency is preserved.

result.name: rounding source
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, one of four outcomes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is handed to the tax engine, which either takes the stored tax amounts as authoritative or recomputes them from the bases.

edge_cases.case: The user typed a tax amount by hand and then changed a quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax line field is protected from recomputation, so the amounts are kept and only the bases move.

edge_cases.case: The user changed the document currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The first condition matches and every tax amount is recomputed from the bases.

edge_cases.case: The user changed only the currency rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The amounts in currency of the tax lines are preserved and only their balances are recomputed as the amount in currency divided by the new rate, rounded to the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The write touched no base line, no tax line and no rate.
edge_cases.outcome: No condition matches and the tax reconciliation stops without doing anything.

edge_cases.case: A changed line carries an explicit amount in currency or balance while the amounts would be kept.
edge_cases.outcome: The reconciliation stops; the caller supplied everything and nothing is recomputed.

worked_examples.description: A foreign-currency invoice whose rate is changed from 1.0850 to 1.1000 while a tax line carries two hundred and ten in the document currency.
worked_examples.narrative: No earlier condition matches, so the source that reapplies the rate is chosen: the amount in currency stays at minus 210.00 and the balance becomes minus 210.00 divided by 1.1000, that is minus 190.909090 and more, rounded to minus 190.91.

worked_examples.description: A quantity is raised on a taxed product line of an invoice in the company currency, with no manual tax amount.

inputs.changed fields: the quantity of one taxed base line

expected_outputs.rounding source: recompute the tax amounts from the bases

worked_examples.narrative: The third condition of the cascade matches; the changed line has taxes now and had them before, the tax line set is unchanged and no field is protected, so the amounts are not kept and the engine recomputes them from the new bases.

records.name: The tax repartition grouping key and the accumulation of the tax line amounts
records.purpose: Decides how many tax lines a document carries and what each one holds, by grouping every repartition contribution of every base line under one key and accumulating the signed amounts under that key.

operands.name: partner of the base line
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: currency of the base line
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: analytic distribution of the base line
operands.source: the base line, unless the tax is not analytic and the repartition line is used in the tax closing, in which case none is carried
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: account
operands.source: the repartition line's account, or, when it has none, the base line's own account
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: taxes propagated onto the tax line
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: tax grids of the repartition line
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: tax repartition line
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: grouped tax
operands.source: the tax group record, when the tax is part of a group
operands.constraints: part of the grouping key

operands.name: tax base amount, amount in currency and balance of the contribution
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the first two, the company currency for the third
operands.source: the rounded tax details the tax engine computed for the base line
operands.constraints: each is multiplied by the base line's sign before it is accumulated

preconditions.condition: The tax engine has computed the rounded tax details of every base line.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to group.

preconditions.condition: The accumulated amounts of a grouping key are not zero in both currencies.
preconditions.otherwise: The grouping key is dropped and no tax line is produced, unless the repartition explicitly asks to keep zero lines.

procedure: Take every repartition contribution of every base line.
Build its grouping key from the partner, the currency, the analytic distribution, the account, the propagated taxes, the tax grids, the repartition line and the grouped tax.
Accumulate under that key the tax base amount, the amount in currency and the balance, each multiplied by the base line's sign.
Drop a grouping key whose accumulated amounts are zero in both currencies, unless the repartition explicitly keeps zero lines.

Return the four lists the engine produces: tax lines to add, tax lines to delete, tax lines to update with their grouping key and their new amounts, and base lines to update with their new tax grids, their new amount in currency and their new balance.
records.formula: tax_line( key ).base = Σ over contributions of ( sign × tax base amount ) ; tax_line( key ).amount_currency = Σ over contributions of ( sign × amount in currency ) ; tax_line( key ).balance = Σ over contributions of ( sign × balance )

rounding.what: Each contribution, before it is accumulated.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the base amount and the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine, which rounds per tax first, then per base line, then distributes the residual difference over the base lines.
rounding.step: Rounding happens inside the engine before the grouping; the accumulation itself adds already-rounded contributions.

result.name: the tax lines of the document
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as journal items with display type `tax`, one per grouping key with a non-zero amount.

edge_cases.case: Two product lines carry the same tax, the same account, the same partner, the same currency and no analytic distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: They share one grouping key and the document carries a single tax line for both.

edge_cases.case: Two product lines carry the same tax but different analytic distributions.
edge_cases.outcome: The keys differ and two tax lines are produced.

edge_cases.case: A grouping key accumulates to zero in both currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: No tax line is produced, unless the repartition explicitly keeps zero lines.

edge_cases.case: The tax is not analytic and the repartition line is used in the tax closing.
edge_cases.outcome: The analytic distribution component of the key is empty, so the tax line carries no analytic distribution.

worked_examples.description: The three-line invoice with two taxes: two lines at twenty-one per cent on the same revenue account and one line at six per cent.
worked_examples.narrative: The two lines at twenty-one per cent share every component of the grouping key, so their contributions of 214.20 and 109.62 accumulate into a single tax line of 323.82, stored with the direction sign of minus one as minus 323.82; the six per cent line forms a second key of 17.94, stored as minus 17.94.

records.name: The non-deductible tax line amount on a purchase document
records.purpose: Books the part of the tax that the company may not deduct, by moving the difference between the tax-included and the tax-excluded totals of the non-deductible base lines onto a dedicated line of the entry.

operands.name: tax-included total of the non-deductible base lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
operands.source: the tax details the engine computed for the base lines flagged as non-deductible
operands.constraints: signed

operands.name: tax-excluded total of the non-deductible base lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
operands.constraints: signed

operands.name: the journal's non-deductible account
operands.source: the journal, falling back to the journal's default account
operands.constraints: must exist for the line to be booked

operands.name: highest line sequence of the document
operands.constraints: the produced line takes a sequence one above it

preconditions.condition: At least one base line of the document is non-deductible.
preconditions.otherwise: Any existing non-deductible tax line is deleted.

preconditions.condition: The document is a purchase document.
preconditions.otherwise: The routine does not apply; a sale document produces no non-deductible line.

procedure: Test whether any base line is still non-deductible; when none is, delete the non-deductible tax line and stop.
Compute the signed difference between the tax-included total and the tax-excluded total of the non-deductible base lines.
Negate that difference to obtain the amount of the line.
Update the existing non-deductible tax line, or create one, on the journal's non-deductible account, or, absent one, the journal's default account.
Label the line “private part (taxes)” and give it a sequence one above the highest line sequence of the document.
records.formula: non_deductible_tax_amount = − ( total_included of the non-deductible base lines − total_excluded of the non-deductible base lines )

rounding.what: The two totals of the non-deductible base lines, before the subtraction.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine when it rounds the tax details.
rounding.step: The totals are already rounded when the difference is taken; the difference itself is not rounded again.

result.name: non-deductible tax line amount
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item with display type `non_deductible_tax`, labelled “private part (taxes)”.

edge_cases.case: No base line is non-deductible any more.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing non-deductible tax line is deleted.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no non-deductible account.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal's default account is used.

edge_cases.case: The document is a sale document.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is produced; deductibility is effective on purchase documents.

worked_examples.description: A purchase document with a base line of one hundred at twenty-one per cent, half of it non-deductible, so the non-deductible base line carries fifty tax-excluded and 60.50 tax-included.
worked_examples.narrative: The difference between the tax-included and the tax-excluded totals is 10.50, and the line carries its negation, minus 10.50, on the journal's non-deductible account, labelled “private part (taxes)”.

records.name: The stored amounts of a base line and the tax engine's rounding delta
records.purpose: Gives a product line the accounting amounts the tax engine computed rather than the plain product of quantity, price and discount, so that the per-line amounts of a tax add up exactly to the rounded total of that tax.

operands.name: tax-excluded total of the line in the document currency
operands.source: the tax engine's rounded detail for the line
operands.constraints: positive in the ordinary case

operands.name: delta on the tax-excluded total in the document currency
operands.source: the residual the tax engine shifted onto this line so that the per-tax totals add up
operands.constraints: usually zero; at most one unit of the last decimal place per line

operands.name: tax-excluded total of the line in the company currency
operands.source: the tax engine's rounded detail for the line
operands.constraints: positive in the ordinary case

operands.name: delta on the tax-excluded total in the company currency
operands.source: the same residual distribution in the company currency
operands.constraints: usually zero

operands.name: direction sign
operands.constraints: plus one or minus one

preconditions.condition: The tax engine has computed and rounded the tax details of the line.
preconditions.otherwise: The stored amounts cannot be derived.

preconditions.condition: The document status is draft.
preconditions.otherwise: The base lines are not updated.

procedure: Take the tax-excluded total the engine computed for the line, in each of the two currencies.
Add the delta the engine allocated to this line in each currency.
Multiply each sum by the direction sign of the document.
Write the first result as the amount in currency of the line and the second as its balance, grouping the updates by currency and by the set of values and writing only where a value actually differs.
records.formula: product_line_amount_currency = sign × ( total_excluded_currency + delta_total_excluded_currency )   and   product_line_balance = sign × ( total_excluded + delta_total_excluded )

rounding.what: The tax-excluded total of each line and the total per tax.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance.
rounding.step: The engine rounds the raw amounts per tax first, then per base line, then distributes the residual difference over the base lines, allocating the remaining units one by one to the largest weights; the delta is that allocation.

result.name: the stored amount in currency and balance of the base line
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item; they are the authoritative accounting amounts, unlike the displayed subtotal and total of the line.

edge_cases.case: The per-line rounded amounts already add up to the rounded total per tax.
edge_cases.outcome: Every delta is zero and the stored amount is the plain rounded tax-excluded total times the direction sign.

edge_cases.case: The per-line rounded amounts fall one unit of the last decimal place short of the rounded total.
edge_cases.outcome: The delta of one unit is allocated to the line with the largest weight, so its stored balance differs from its displayed subtotal by that unit.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one and the stored amount is positive, a debit.

worked_examples.description: Two lines of a price-included tax at twenty-one per cent with a unit price of 21.53 each, on a two-decimal currency, with global rounding.
worked_examples.narrative: The rounded total of 35.59 exceeds the sum of the two rounded lines by 0.01, so the delta of one hundredth is added to the first line; the stored balances become 17.80 and 17.79 while both displayed subtotals stay at 17.79.

worked_examples.description: The three-line invoice with two taxes, where the shares already add up.

expected_outputs.stored amounts: the plain rounded tax-excluded totals times the direction sign

worked_examples.narrative: The two shares add to exactly 323.82, so no unit is shifted and the delta is zero.

records.name: The line subtotal and the line total shown while the document is edited
records.purpose: Gives the line list a figure on every keystroke, before the document is saved and before the synchronisation runs, so that the user sees the effect of a change immediately.

operands.name: quantity of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: unit price of the line
operands.constraints: may be negative

operands.name: discount of the line
operands.constraints: between zero and one hundred in the ordinary case

operands.name: taxes of the line
operands.constraints: the tax engine is run on this single line alone

operands.name: rounding method of the company
operands.constraints: the same method the engine uses for the document

preconditions.condition: The line carries a quantity, a unit price and its set of taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: Both values are zero.

procedure: Run the tax engine on this single line alone, with the company's rounding method.
Take the tax-excluded total in the document currency as the line subtotal.
Take the tax-included total in the document currency as the line total.
Store both and show them in the line list; they are display values and are not the authoritative accounting amounts.
records.formula: price_subtotal = total_excluded_currency of the line's own tax computation   and   price_total = total_included_currency of the line's own tax computation

rounding.what: The tax-excluded and the tax-included totals of the single line.
rounding.precision: The document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, with the company's rounding method applied by the tax engine.
rounding.step: Inside the single-line tax computation, on every keystroke, independently of the synchronisation.

result.name: the line subtotal and the line total
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the line and shown in the line list; the authoritative accounting amounts are the balance and the amount in currency the synchronisation produces.

edge_cases.case: The tax engine shifted a rounding delta onto this line when the whole document was computed.
edge_cases.outcome: The displayed subtotal keeps the per-line figure while the stored balance carries the delta, so the two differ by one unit of the last decimal place.

edge_cases.case: The line carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtotal and the total are equal.

edge_cases.case: The line is a section, a subsection or a note.
edge_cases.outcome: Both values are zero, as such a line has no amount.

worked_examples.description: A line of forty printed manuals at 14.50 with a discount of ten per cent and a tax of twenty-one per cent.
worked_examples.narrative: Forty times 14.50 times 0.90 is 522.00, and 522.00 times 1.21 is 631.62; both are shown in the line list on every keystroke.

worked_examples.description: One of the two price-included lines of the rounding-delta example.
worked_examples.narrative: The single-line computation gives 17.79 tax-excluded and 21.53 tax-included, and both stay at those values in the list even though the first line's stored balance carries the delta of 0.01.

records.name: Due date of a payment term line with the delay type days after invoice date
records.purpose: Gives one instalment its maturity date when the term counts a plain number of days from the reference date, which is the ordinary net-days term.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the document date, else the accounting date, else today
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: day count of the payment term line
operands.source: the day count field of the payment term line
operands.constraints: zero or a positive whole number in the ordinary case

preconditions.condition: The payment term line carries the delay type that counts days after the invoice date.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the three other delay types applies and its own rule is used.

preconditions.condition: A reference date is available.
preconditions.otherwise: Today is used, because the reference date always falls back to today.

procedure: Take the reference date.
Add the day count of the payment term line to it, counting whole calendar days across month and year boundaries.
The result is the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = reference_date + day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole calendar days.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the maturity date of the payment term line and used as part of the key of the needed terms.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the reference date itself, which is what an immediate term produces.

edge_cases.case: The addition crosses a month or a year boundary.
edge_cases.outcome: The calendar days are counted through, so the result may fall in a later month or year.

edge_cases.case: The addition crosses the end of February in a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The twenty-ninth of February counts as a day like any other.

worked_examples.description: An immediate line on an invoice dated the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: Adding zero days leaves the reference date unchanged, so the instalment falls due the same day.

worked_examples.description: A forty-five day line on the same invoice.
worked_examples.narrative: Eleven days remain in January, February contributes twenty-eight days in the year 2026, and the remaining six days fall in March, so the maturity date is the sixth of March.

records.name: Due date of a payment term line with the delay type days after end of month
records.purpose: Gives one instalment its maturity date when the term first moves to the end of the month of the reference date and then counts days, which is the ordinary end-of-month term.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the document date, else the accounting date, else today
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: day count of the payment term line
operands.source: the day count field of the payment term line
operands.constraints: zero or a positive whole number in the ordinary case

preconditions.condition: The payment term line carries the delay type that counts days after the end of the month.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the three other delay types applies.

preconditions.condition: A reference date is available.
preconditions.otherwise: Today is used.

procedure: Take the reference date and find the last day of its month.
Add the day count of the payment term line to that last day, counting whole calendar days.
The result is the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = ( last day of the month of reference_date ) + day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole calendar days.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the maturity date of the payment term line.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the last day of the month of the reference date.

edge_cases.case: The month of the reference date is February of a year that is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The last day is the twenty-eighth.

edge_cases.case: The addition of the day count crosses into the following month.
edge_cases.outcome: The calendar days are counted through, so the maturity date falls in that later month.

worked_examples.description: A line with no additional days on an invoice dated the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The last day of January is the thirty-first, and no day is added.

worked_examples.description: A line of fifteen days after the end of the month on the same invoice.
worked_examples.narrative: The thirty-first of January plus fifteen days is the fifteenth of February.

records.name: Due date of a payment term line with the delay type days after end of next month
records.purpose: Gives one instalment its maturity date when the term first moves to the end of the month following the reference date and then counts days.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the document date, else the accounting date, else today
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: day count of the payment term line
operands.source: the day count field of the payment term line
operands.constraints: zero or a positive whole number in the ordinary case

preconditions.condition: The payment term line carries the delay type that counts days after the end of the next month.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the three other delay types applies.

preconditions.condition: A reference date is available.
preconditions.otherwise: Today is used.

procedure: Take the reference date and find the month that follows its month.
Find the last day of that following month.
Add the day count of the payment term line to that last day, counting whole calendar days.
The result is the maturity date of the instalment.
records.formula: due_date = ( last day of the month following the month of reference_date ) + day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole calendar days.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the maturity date of the payment term line.

edge_cases.case: The reference date falls in December.
edge_cases.outcome: The following month is January of the next year and the maturity date falls in that next year.

edge_cases.case: The following month is February of a year that is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The last day is the twenty-eighth, as in the worked example.

edge_cases.case: The day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the last day of the following month.

worked_examples.description: A line with no additional days on an invoice dated the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The month following January is February, whose last day in the year 2026 is the twenty-eighth, and no day is added.

records.name: Due date of a payment term line with the delay type days end of month on a given day of month
records.purpose: Gives one instalment its maturity date when the term counts days, then moves forward one month and lands on a fixed day of that month, which is the term used where invoices are settled on a fixed payment day.

operands.name: reference date
operands.source: the document date, else the accounting date, else today
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: day count of the payment term line
operands.source: the day count field of the payment term line
operands.constraints: zero or a positive whole number in the ordinary case

operands.name: day of month on which the instalment falls
operands.source: the text field that names the day in the next month, read as a whole number; when the text cannot be read as a whole number it is taken as one
operands.constraints: when it is zero or negative the rule changes to the last day of the month

preconditions.condition: The payment term line carries the delay type that lands on a given day of the month.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the three other delay types applies.

preconditions.condition: The text naming the day of month can be read as a whole number.
preconditions.otherwise: The day of month is taken as one.

procedure: Read the day of month as a whole number, taking one when the text cannot be read as a whole number.
When the day of month is zero or negative, add the day count to the reference date and take the last day of the month of the result; the maturity date is that last day.
Otherwise add the day count to the reference date.
Move the result forward by exactly one month.
Set the day of month of that date to the day of month read in the first step.
When the target month is shorter than the day of month, use the last day of the target month instead.
records.formula: if day_of_month ≤ 0 : due_date = last day of the month of ( reference_date + day_count days ) ; else : due_date = ( reference_date + day_count days ) moved forward one month, with the day of month set to day_of_month, clamped to the last day of the target month

rounding.what: Only the clamping of the day of month to the length of the target month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.method: The day of month is reduced to the last day of the target month when the target month is shorter.
rounding.step: After the month has been advanced and before the maturity date is stored.

result.name: maturity date of the instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the maturity date of the payment term line.

edge_cases.case: The day of month is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the last day of the month of the reference date plus the day count, and no month is added.

edge_cases.case: The day of month is thirty-one and the target month is April.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the thirtieth of April, the last day of the target month.

edge_cases.case: The day of month is thirty and the target month is February of a year that is not a leap year.
edge_cases.outcome: The maturity date is the twenty-eighth of February.

edge_cases.case: The text naming the day of month is empty or not a number.
edge_cases.outcome: The day of month is taken as one, so the maturity date is the first of the target month.

worked_examples.description: No additional days and a payment day of the tenth, on an invoice dated the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: Adding zero days leaves the twentieth of January, adding one month gives the twentieth of February, and setting the day of month to ten gives the tenth of February.

worked_examples.description: Fifteen days and a payment day of the tenth, on the same invoice.
worked_examples.narrative: Adding fifteen days gives the fourth of February, adding one month gives the fourth of March, and setting the day of month to ten gives the tenth of March.

worked_examples.description: Ten days and a payment day of zero, on the same invoice.
worked_examples.narrative: The day of month is not greater than zero, so no month is added and the maturity date is the last day of the month of the thirtieth of January, that is the thirty-first of January.

records.name: The signed totals handed to the payment term distribution by a stored document
records.purpose: Turns the customer-facing totals of a document that already exists in the database into the accounting-signed totals the payment term distribution works on, so that the instalments carry the sign the receivable line must have.

operands.name: stored customer-facing tax total
operands.source: the tax total field of the document
operands.constraints: positive on a customer invoice and on a customer credit note alike

operands.name: stored signed tax total
operands.source: the signed tax total field of the document
operands.constraints: carries the reporting sign

operands.name: stored customer-facing net total
operands.source: the untaxed total field of the document
operands.constraints: positive on a customer invoice and on a customer credit note alike

operands.name: stored signed net total
operands.source: the signed untaxed total field of the document
operands.constraints: carries the reporting sign

operands.name: inbound indication
operands.source: the document type: a customer invoice, a sales receipt or a vendor credit note is inbound
operands.constraints: decides the value of the sign parameter

preconditions.condition: The document is stored, so its lines have database identifiers.
preconditions.otherwise: The totals are recomputed from scratch by the branch for a document not yet stored.

preconditions.condition: The document is an invoice and has invoice lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The needed terms are empty and no payment term line is produced.

procedure: Let the sign parameter be plus one when the document is inbound, receipts included, and minus one otherwise.
Multiply the stored customer-facing tax total by the sign parameter to obtain the tax amount in the document currency.
Take the stored signed tax total as the tax amount in the company currency.
Multiply the stored customer-facing net total by the sign parameter to obtain the untaxed amount in the document currency.
Take the stored signed net total as the untaxed amount in the company currency.
Hand the same sign parameter to the distribution, where it is consumed only by fixed-amount payment term lines.
records.formula: s = +1 when the document is inbound, −1 otherwise ; tax_amount_currency = s × stored customer-facing tax total ; tax_amount = stored signed tax total ; untaxed_amount_currency = s × stored customer-facing net total ; untaxed_amount = stored signed net total

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded here; the stored totals are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the amounts in currency, the company currency for the others.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the totals were computed.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the four accounting-signed totals handed to the distribution
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency for two of them, the company currency for the other two
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the distribution, which produces the payment term lines.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign parameter is plus one, all four amounts are positive, and each instalment is a debit on the receivable account.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign parameter is minus one, all four amounts are negative, and each instalment is a credit.

edge_cases.case: The document has no invoice line.
edge_cases.outcome: The needed terms are empty and no receivable line is produced.

worked_examples.description: A stored customer invoice with a net total of one thousand and a tax of twenty-one per cent, in the company currency.
worked_examples.narrative: The document is inbound, so the sign parameter is plus one and the accounting-signed totals coincide with the customer-facing ones; the total handed to the distribution is 1 210.00.

worked_examples.description: A stored customer credit note of the same size.
worked_examples.narrative: The document is outbound, so the sign parameter is minus one, the totals are negative and each instalment is a credit of the corresponding amount.

records.name: The signed totals recomputed for a document that is not yet stored
records.purpose: Supplies the payment term distribution with totals while a new document is still being typed in the form and its lines have no database identifiers, so that the instalments shown on screen already match the ones that will be stored.

operands.name: base line updates from the tax engine
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
operands.source: the tax engine, called on base lines built as for the tax reconciliation but without taking any existing tax line as authoritative
operands.constraints: one per product line, plus the synthesised early payment discount and non-deductible base lines

operands.name: tax lines to add from the tax engine
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency for the amount in currency, the company currency for the balance
operands.constraints: one per tax repartition grouping key

operands.name: direction sign
operands.constraints: plus one or minus one; it is the sign parameter in this branch

preconditions.condition: The document is not yet stored.
preconditions.otherwise: The stored totals are used instead.

preconditions.condition: The tax engine can be called on the synthesised base lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The totals cannot be recomputed.

procedure: Build the base lines and the tax lines as for the tax reconciliation, but without taking existing tax lines as authoritative.
Add the accounting data and prepare the tax lines.
Sum the direction sign times the amount in currency over the base line updates to obtain the untaxed amount in the document currency.
Sum the direction sign times the balance over the base line updates to obtain the untaxed amount in the company currency.
Sum the direction sign times the amount in currency over the tax lines to add to obtain the tax amount in the document currency.
Sum the direction sign times the balance over the tax lines to add to obtain the tax amount in the company currency.
Hand the direction sign itself to the distribution as the sign parameter, which is the opposite of the parameter used for a stored document.
records.formula: untaxed_amount_currency = Σ over base line updates of ( s × amount_currency ) ; untaxed_amount = Σ over base line updates of ( s × balance ) ; tax_amount_currency = Σ over tax lines to add of ( s × amount_currency ) ; tax_amount = Σ over tax lines to add of ( s × balance ), with s the direction sign

rounding.what: The amounts of the base line updates and of the tax lines to add.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the amounts in currency, the company currency for the balances.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine.
rounding.step: Inside the tax engine, before the sums are taken; the sums themselves are not rounded again.

result.name: the four accounting-signed totals handed to the distribution
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency for two of them, the company currency for the other two
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the distribution while the form is open.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: A base line's amount in currency is the direction sign times the tax-excluded total, so multiplying by the direction sign again yields a positive figure, matching the stored case.

edge_cases.case: The payment term mixes a fixed-amount line with other lines while the document is unsaved.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign parameter differs from the stored case, and the difference is observable on the fixed-amount line only.

edge_cases.case: The early payment discount lines and the non-deductible lines do not exist as records yet.
edge_cases.outcome: Equivalent base lines are synthesised from the needed maps of the product lines.

worked_examples.description: A new customer invoice being typed, with one product line of one thousand at twenty-one per cent in the company currency.
worked_examples.narrative: The base line's stored amount is minus 1 000.00 because the direction sign of a customer invoice is minus one; multiplying by the direction sign again gives plus 1 000.00, and the tax gives plus 210.00, so the total is 1 210.00, the same figure the stored branch produces, while the sign parameter is minus one instead of plus one.

records.name: The distribution totals and the effective currency rate
records.purpose: Derives the two totals the instalments are cut from and the rate that converts between them, using a rate read from the totals themselves so that the instalments add up exactly in both currencies.

operands.name: tax amount in the company currency
operands.constraints: accounting-signed

operands.name: untaxed amount in the company currency
operands.constraints: accounting-signed

operands.name: tax amount in the document currency
operands.constraints: accounting-signed

operands.name: untaxed amount in the document currency
operands.constraints: accounting-signed

preconditions.condition: The total in the company currency is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The effective rate is taken as zero, and the fixed-amount and cash-rounding branches that divide by it produce zero.
