records.name: The scope within which the next number is sought
records.purpose: Defines the set of existing numbers a new number must follow, since the sequence is not a counter but the highest number matching a scope.

operands.name: journal of the document
operands.constraints: the scope is always restricted to the same journal

operands.name: dedicated credit note sequence flag of the journal
operands.constraints: when set, credit notes are numbered among credit notes and everything else among everything else

operands.name: dedicated payment sequence flag of the journal
operands.constraints: when set, payments are numbered among payments and non-payments among non-payments

operands.name: dedicated debit note sequence flag of the journal
operands.constraints: when set, debit notes are numbered among debit notes and non-debit-notes among non-debit-notes

operands.name: self-billing indication of the journal
operands.constraints: when set, the scope is restricted to the same commercial entity

operands.name: accounting date of the document
operands.constraints: must fall inside the period implied by the detected reset rule

preconditions.condition: The journal is known.
preconditions.otherwise: No scope can be formed and no number can be sought.

procedure: Restrict to documents of the same journal.
Exclude documents whose number is the placeholder `/`.
When the journal has a dedicated credit note sequence, restrict to the same side: credit notes among credit notes and everything else among everything else.
When the journal has a dedicated payment sequence, restrict payments to payments and non-payments to non-payments.
When the journal has a dedicated debit note sequence, restrict debit notes to debit notes and non-debit-notes to non-debit-notes.
When the journal is a self-billing journal, restrict to the same commercial entity, and treat the scope as empty when there is no partner, which forces a fresh start.
Restrict to accounting dates inside the period implied by the detected reset rule.
records.formula: scope = same journal , number ≠ `/` , same side when a dedicated credit note sequence exists , same payment kind when a dedicated payment sequence exists , same debit note kind when a dedicated debit note sequence exists , same commercial entity on a self-billing journal , accounting date inside the period of the detected reset rule

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a set of documents.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the scope of the sequence
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a set of existing numbers
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the highest number of the scope is the one the new number must follow.

edge_cases.case: The journal is a self-billing journal and the document has no partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The scope is empty, which forces a fresh start from a newly built starting number.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no dedicated credit note sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: Credit notes and invoices are numbered in one series.

edge_cases.case: No number exists in the scope.
edge_cases.outcome: A starting number is built.

worked_examples.description: A customer credit note in a sale journal with a dedicated credit note sequence, in a calendar fiscal year.
worked_examples.narrative: The dedicated credit note sequence restricts the scope to credit notes, so the invoice number is excluded and the next credit note follows the highest credit note number.

records.name: Detecting the reset rule and the anti-pattern that protects a stricter number
records.purpose: Reads from an existing number how often the counter restarts, and keeps a looser grammar from matching a number that belongs to a stricter one.

operands.name: reference number
operands.source: the last number at or before this document's date inside the scope, and failing that the first number in the scope
operands.constraints: the grammar is read from it

operands.name: number pattern of the journal
operands.constraints: when the journal defines its own pattern, that pattern overrides the built-in grammars

operands.name: detected reset rule
operands.source: the grammar of the reference number
operands.constraints: one of never, yearly, monthly, by fiscal year range, and by fiscal year range and month

preconditions.condition: A reference number exists in the scope.
preconditions.otherwise: No reset rule can be deduced and a starting number is built.

preconditions.condition: The journal defines no number pattern of its own.
preconditions.otherwise: That pattern overrides the built-in grammars.

procedure: Take as the reference number the last number at or before this document's date inside the scope, and, failing that, the first number in the scope.
Read the grammar of that number to deduce the reset rule among never, yearly, monthly, by fiscal year range, and by fiscal year range and month.
Apply the anti-pattern: when the reset rule is yearly or by fiscal year range, exclude numbers whose prefix matches the monthly grammar.
Apply the anti-pattern: when the reset rule is never, exclude numbers whose prefix matches the yearly grammar, which also excludes the monthly grammar and the two range grammars.
Let the journal's own number pattern override the built-in grammars when one is defined.
records.formula: reset rule = the rule read from the reference number's grammar ; anti-pattern : reset rule yearly or by fiscal year range → exclude numbers whose prefix matches the monthly grammar ; reset rule never → exclude numbers whose prefix matches the yearly grammar, and therefore also the monthly grammar and the two range grammars

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a rule and a filter.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the reset rule and the filtered scope
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; they decide which numbers count as the predecessors of the new one.

edge_cases.case: The journal defines its own number pattern.
edge_cases.outcome: That pattern overrides the built-in grammars entirely.

edge_cases.case: A yearly number and a monthly number coexist in the journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The anti-pattern excludes the monthly ones while a yearly reset rule is in force, so the looser grammar does not swallow the stricter numbers.

edge_cases.case: The reset rule is never.
edge_cases.outcome: Numbers whose prefix matches the yearly grammar are excluded, which also excludes the monthly grammar and the two fiscal-year-range grammars.

worked_examples.description: A journal whose existing numbers follow the yearly grammar with a four-digit year.

expected_outputs.numbers excluded by the anti-pattern: every number whose prefix matches the monthly grammar

worked_examples.narrative: The reference number names a year and a counter, so the reset rule is yearly; any number that also names a month is excluded from the scope, and the next number continues the yearly series.

records.name: The year part of a starting number
records.purpose: Builds the year component of the first number of a scope, which is a four-digit year on a calendar fiscal year and a two-digit range on a staggered one.

operands.name: date used for the number
operands.source: the accounting date, else the document date, else today
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: fiscal year end of the company
operands.constraints: the day is clamped to the number of days in the fiscal year end month

preconditions.condition: The company's fiscal year end is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The calendar convention applies and the year part is the four-digit year.

procedure: Take the accounting date, else the document date, else today, and call it the date used for the number.
When the company's fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December, take the four-digit year of that date.
Otherwise clamp the fiscal year end day to the number of days in the fiscal year end month.
When the date is after the fiscal year end of its own calendar year, form the range from the two-digit year of the date and the two-digit year of the date plus one.
Otherwise form the range from the two-digit year of the date less one and the two-digit year of the date.
records.formula: year part = the four-digit year of D when the fiscal year ends on 31 December ; otherwise the two-digit range ( two-digit year of D )-( two-digit year of D + 1 ) when D is after the fiscal year end of its own calendar year, and ( two-digit year of D − 1 )-( two-digit year of D ) otherwise, where D is the accounting date, else the document date, else today

rounding.what: Only the clamping of the fiscal year end day to the length of its month.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.method: The day is reduced to the last day of the fiscal year end month when the month is shorter.
rounding.step: Before the comparison of the date with the fiscal year end.

result.name: the year part of the starting number
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a reproduced identifier component
result.stored_or_displayed: Part of the number stored on the document.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December.
edge_cases.outcome: The year part is the four-digit year and the counter keeps its five digits.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year ends on the thirtieth of June and the date is the fifteenth of March.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is before the fiscal year end of its own calendar year, so the range is formed from the previous two-digit year and the current one.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year end day is the thirty-first of a month that has thirty days.
edge_cases.outcome: The day is clamped to the last day of that month.

worked_examples.description: A calendar fiscal year and a document dated the fifteenth of March of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The fiscal year ends on the thirty-first of December, so the year part is the four-digit year.

worked_examples.description: A fiscal year ending on the thirtieth of June and a document dated the fifteenth of March of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The fifteenth of March comes before the thirtieth of June of the same calendar year, so the range runs from the previous two-digit year to the current one.

records.name: The starting number of a sale, bank, cash or credit journal
records.purpose: Builds the first number of a scope for the journals whose numbers name only a year, which is the shape a customer invoice number takes.

operands.name: journal code
operands.constraints: the first component of the number

operands.name: year part
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a reproduced identifier component
operands.constraints: four digits on a calendar fiscal year, a two-digit range otherwise

operands.name: fiscal year staggering
operands.constraints: shortens the counter from five digits to four

preconditions.condition: The journal is of the sale, bank, cash or credit kind.
preconditions.otherwise: The starting number of any other journal applies, which also names the month.

preconditions.condition: No number exists in the scope.
preconditions.otherwise: The next number continues from the highest existing number instead.

procedure: Take the journal code.
Append a solidus and the year part.
Append a solidus and a counter of five zeros, shortened to four zeros when the fiscal year is staggered, so that the number stays short.
Give the first document of the scope the number that follows this starting number.
records.formula: starting number = journal code + `/` + year part + `/` + `00000` , the counter shortened to `0000` when the fiscal year is staggered

rounding.what: Nothing; the counter is a fixed width of digits.
rounding.precision: Five digits, or four on a staggered fiscal year.
rounding.step: When the starting number is built.

result.name: the starting number
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored itself; the first real document of the scope takes the number that follows it.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year is staggered.
edge_cases.outcome: The counter is four digits rather than five, to keep the number short beside the longer year range.

edge_cases.case: The journal has a dedicated credit note, payment or debit note sequence and the document is of that kind.
edge_cases.outcome: The corresponding letter is prefixed to the journal code.

edge_cases.case: The journal is a self-billing journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The commercial entity's identifier padded to five digits is appended to the journal code.

worked_examples.description: A sale journal with a calendar fiscal year and a document dated the fifteenth of March of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The starting number carries a counter of five zeros, so the first document of the scope takes the number that follows it.

worked_examples.description: The same journal in a company whose fiscal year ends on the thirtieth of June, with a document dated the fifteenth of March of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The year part is a two-digit range and the counter is shortened to four digits.

records.name: The starting number of any journal that is not a sale, bank, cash or credit journal
records.purpose: Builds the first number of a scope for the journals whose numbers name both a year and a month, and appends the commercial entity on a self-billing journal.

operands.name: journal code
operands.constraints: the first component of the number

operands.name: year part
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a reproduced identifier component
operands.constraints: four digits or a two-digit range

operands.name: month of the date used for the number
operands.source: the accounting date, else the document date, else today
operands.constraints: written with two digits

operands.name: commercial entity identifier
operands.source: the partner of a self-billing document
operands.constraints: padded to five digits and appended to the journal code

preconditions.condition: The journal is not of the sale, bank, cash or credit kind.
preconditions.otherwise: The shorter starting number applies.

preconditions.condition: No number exists in the scope.
preconditions.otherwise: The next number continues from the highest existing number.

procedure: Take the journal code, and on a self-billing journal append the commercial entity's identifier padded to five digits.
Append a solidus and the year part.
Append a solidus and the two-digit month of the date used for the number.
Append a solidus and a counter of four zeros.
records.formula: starting number = journal code + `/` + year part + `/` + two-digit month + `/` + `0000` , with the commercial entity's identifier padded to five digits appended to the journal code on a self-billing journal

rounding.what: Nothing; the month and the counter are fixed widths of digits.
rounding.precision: Two digits for the month, four for the counter, five for the appended entity identifier.
rounding.step: When the starting number is built.

result.name: the starting number
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored itself; the first document of the scope takes the number that follows it.

edge_cases.case: The journal is a self-billing journal with no partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The scope is empty and a fresh starting number is built, but the entity component cannot be formed, so the scope forces a fresh start.

edge_cases.case: The month is a single digit.
edge_cases.outcome: It is written with two digits, so March is written as the two characters that spell zero three.

edge_cases.case: The fiscal year is staggered.
edge_cases.outcome: The year part is a two-digit range while the counter keeps four digits.

records.name: The letter prefixes of a credit note, a payment and a debit note
records.purpose: Marks a number as belonging to a dedicated series by prefixing a letter to the journal code, so that credit notes, payments and debit notes are recognisable and numbered apart.

operands.name: dedicated payment sequence flag of the journal
operands.constraints: the letter `P` is prefixed to a payment's number

operands.name: document type
operands.constraints: decides which prefix applies

Prefix the letter `D` when the journal has a dedicated debit note sequence and the document is a debit note of a customer invoice or a vendor bill.

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is an identifier.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the prefixed number

records.name: The accounting date correction of a sale document dated in a closed period
records.purpose: Pushes the accounting date of a sale document forward when a lock date is violated, so that the number the document takes stays in increasing order.

operands.name: last violated lock date
operands.source: the lock dates of the company
operands.constraints: the candidate date becomes the day after it

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: caps the corrected date

operands.name: highest number in the scope
operands.source: the scope, or, absent that, the last number found with the relaxed scope
operands.constraints: may be absent

operands.name: reset rule
operands.constraints: monthly or yearly change the correction

preconditions.condition: A lock date is violated.
preconditions.otherwise: On a sale document no correction is applied and the candidate date stands.

preconditions.condition: The document is a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The correction for a non-sale document applies, which runs whether or not a lock date was violated.

procedure: Set the candidate date to the last violated lock date plus one day.
When there is no highest number, or the reset rule is monthly, take the earlier of today and the last day of the candidate date's month.
When the reset rule is yearly, take the earlier of today and the last day of the candidate date's year.
Otherwise let the candidate date stand.
records.formula: candidate = last violated lock date + 1 day ; no highest number or reset rule monthly → result = min( today , last day of the candidate's month ) ; reset rule yearly → result = min( today , last day of the candidate's year ) ; otherwise result = candidate

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole calendar days.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the corrected accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the accounting date of the document, from which the number is then built.

edge_cases.case: No lock date is violated.
edge_cases.outcome: No correction is applied to a sale document.

edge_cases.case: There is no highest number in the scope.
edge_cases.outcome: The monthly branch is used, so the date is capped at the last day of the candidate's month or at today, whichever comes first.

edge_cases.case: Today falls before the last day of the candidate's month.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is taken, so the document is not dated in the future.

worked_examples.description: A sale document whose accounting date falls in a period locked to the thirty-first of January of the year 2026, in a journal whose reset rule is monthly, with today being the tenth of February of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate is the first of February, and the earlier of today and the last day of February is today, so the document is dated the tenth of February.

worked_examples.description: The same document in a journal whose reset rule is yearly, with today being the tenth of February of the year 2027.
worked_examples.narrative: The earlier of today and the thirty-first of December of the candidate's year is that thirty-first of December, so the document is dated at the end of the year the lock date closed.

records.name: The accounting date correction of a document that is not a sale document
records.purpose: Adjusts the accounting date of a document outside the sale journals so that its number keeps the order of the series, whether or not a lock date was violated.

operands.name: candidate date
operands.source: the last violated lock date plus one day when a lock date is violated, otherwise the document's own accounting date
operands.constraints: always defined

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: compared with the candidate by year and by month

operands.name: highest number in the scope
operands.source: the scope, or the last number found with the relaxed scope
operands.constraints: may be absent

operands.name: reset rule
operands.constraints: monthly, fiscal-year-range monthly or yearly change the correction

preconditions.condition: The document is not a sale document.
preconditions.otherwise: The correction for a sale document applies, which runs only on a lock violation.

procedure: Set the candidate date to the last violated lock date plus one day when a lock date is violated.

When there is no highest number, or the reset rule is monthly or fiscal-year-range monthly, compare today's year and month with the candidate's: when today is later, take the last day of the candidate's month, and otherwise take the later of the candidate and today.

When the reset rule is yearly, compare today's year with the candidate's: when today's year is later, take the thirty-first of December of the candidate's year, and otherwise take the later of the candidate and today.
Otherwise let the candidate date stand.
records.formula: no highest number, or reset rule monthly or fiscal-year-range monthly → result = last day of the candidate's month when today's ( year , month ) is after the candidate's, otherwise max( candidate , today ) ; reset rule yearly → result = 31 December of the candidate's year when today's year is after the candidate's, otherwise max( candidate , today ) ; otherwise result = candidate

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole calendar days.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the corrected accounting date
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the accounting date of the document.

edge_cases.case: No lock date is violated.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction still runs on a non-sale document, unlike on a sale document.

edge_cases.case: Today falls in the same month as the candidate.

records.name: The two check digits of a structured creditor reference
records.purpose: Computes the two digits that let a bank verify a structured creditor reference before it is used to match a payment, using the same modulo arithmetic as an international bank account number.

operands.name: data of the reference
operands.source: the concatenation the generator built, either the journal code and the padded document identifier, or the journal code and the customer's digits
operands.constraints: letters and digits of the basic Latin set

operands.name: the two literal characters that name the standard
operands.constraints: appended to the data before the arithmetic

preconditions.condition: The data consists of letters and digits only.
preconditions.otherwise: The letter-to-digit substitution is not defined for the other characters.

procedure: Append the two literal characters that name the standard to the data.

Replace every letter by two digits, the first letter of the alphabet becoming ten, each following letter one more than the one before it, and therefore the last letter becoming thirty-five; leave every digit as it is.
Read the whole result as one decimal whole number.
Multiply that number by one hundred and take the remainder modulo ninety-seven.

Subtract the remainder from ninety-eight to obtain the check number; equivalently, the check number is the two-digit value that makes the number times one hundred plus the check number leave a remainder of one modulo ninety-seven.
Format the check number with two digits, padding with a leading zero when needed.
records.formula: V = the decimal whole number read from the data with `RF` appended and every letter replaced by its two-digit rank from 10 for `A` to 35 for `Z` ; check number c = 98 − ( V × 100 mod 97 ) , equivalently the two-digit c with ( V × 100 + c ) mod 97 = 1 ; c is written with two digits

rounding.what: Nothing; the arithmetic is on whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Two digits for the check number.
rounding.method: Left-padded with a leading zero when the check number is below ten.
rounding.step: After the subtraction from ninety-eight.

result.name: the two check digits
result.stored_or_displayed: Placed immediately after the two literal characters that name the standard, at the head of the reference.

edge_cases.case: The check number is below ten.
edge_cases.outcome: It is written with a leading zero, so that the reference always carries two check digits.

edge_cases.case: The remainder is ninety-six.
edge_cases.outcome: The check number is two, written with a leading zero.

edge_cases.case: The data contains a letter outside the basic Latin set.
edge_cases.outcome: The generator uses the journal's internal identifier instead of the journal code, so the data stays within the basic Latin set.

worked_examples.description: The data built from a journal code and a document identifier of thirty-seven.
worked_examples.narrative: The three letters of the journal code become eighteen, twenty-three and thirty-one, the two characters of the standard become twenty-seven and fifteen, the whole number is 1 823 310 000 372 715, its product by one hundred leaves a remainder of thirty-one modulo ninety-seven, and ninety-eight less thirty-one is sixty-seven.

worked_examples.description: The data built from a journal code and a customer's digits.
worked_examples.narrative: The whole number is 1 823 316 542 715, its product by one hundred leaves a remainder of eighty-two, and ninety-eight less eighty-two is sixteen.

records.name: The payment reference in the European standard, based on the invoice
records.purpose: Builds the structured creditor reference from the journal and the document, so that a bank can validate the communication and the incoming line can be matched without ambiguity.

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the journal, when the code is made only of alphanumeric characters of the basic Latin set
operands.constraints: otherwise the journal's internal identifier is used

operands.name: internal identifier of the document
operands.constraints: left-padded with zeros to six digits

operands.name: check digits
operands.constraints: two digits

preconditions.condition: The journal code is made only of alphanumeric characters of the basic Latin set.
preconditions.otherwise: The journal's internal identifier is used in its place.

procedure: Take the journal code when it is purely alphanumeric in the basic Latin set, and the journal's internal identifier otherwise.
Left-pad the document's internal identifier with zeros to six digits.
Concatenate the two to form the data.
Compute the two check digits over that data.
Write the two literal characters that name the standard, then the two check digits, then a space, then the data split into groups of four characters separated by spaces.
records.formula: data = J + N , where J is the journal code or the journal's internal identifier and N is the document's internal identifier left-padded with zeros to six digits ; reference = `RF` + the two check digits + a space + the data in groups of four separated by spaces

rounding.what: Nothing; the padding is to a fixed width.
rounding.precision: Six digits for the document identifier, two for the check digits.
rounding.step: Before the data is concatenated and before the check digits are computed.

result.name: payment reference
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document, printed as the communication to quote, and embedded in the quick response code payload when the code generator supports a structured communication.

edge_cases.outcome: The journal's internal identifier is used instead of the code.

edge_cases.case: The data does not divide into whole groups of four.

records.name: The payment reference in the European standard, based on the customer
records.purpose: Builds the structured creditor reference from the journal and the customer, so that every payment from that customer carries the same validated communication.

operands.name: journal code
operands.source: the journal, when the code is purely alphanumeric in the basic Latin set
operands.constraints: otherwise the journal's internal identifier is used

operands.name: internal reference of the partner
operands.constraints: only its digits are kept, and only the last twenty-one characters of those

operands.name: partner identifier
operands.constraints: used when the partner has no internal reference; its last twenty-one characters are taken

preconditions.condition: The document has a partner.
preconditions.otherwise: No customer-based reference can be built.

procedure: Take the journal code when it is purely alphanumeric in the basic Latin set, and the journal's internal identifier otherwise.

Take the partner's internal reference, keep only its digits and take the last twenty-one characters; when the partner has no internal reference, take the last twenty-one characters of the partner identifier instead.
Prepend the journal code to that string and take the last twenty-one characters of the result to form the data.
Compute the two check digits over that data.
Write the two literal characters that name the standard, then the two check digits, then a space, then the data split into groups of four characters separated by spaces.
records.formula: digits = the digits of the partner's internal reference, last 21 characters, or the last 21 characters of the partner identifier when there is no reference ; data = the last 21 characters of ( J + digits ) ; reference = `RF` + the two check digits + a space + the data in groups of four separated by spaces

rounding.what: Nothing; the truncation is to a fixed width.
rounding.precision: Twenty-one characters for the data, two digits for the check digits.
rounding.method: The last twenty-one characters are kept.
rounding.step: Twice: once on the customer's digits and once on the concatenation with the journal code.

result.name: payment reference
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and printed as the communication to quote.

edge_cases.outcome: Only its last twenty-one characters are kept, which may cut into the journal code.

edge_cases.case: The partner's internal reference contains letters and spaces.

records.name: Building the ordered instalment list of a document
records.purpose: Turns the payment term lines of a document into a numbered list carrying, for each instalment, what is outstanding and in which state it stands, which is what the portal and the payment registration read.

operands.name: payment term lines of the document
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
operands.constraints: sorted by maturity date, a missing maturity date sorting last, then by accounting date

operands.name: payment currency
operands.constraints: used by the eligibility test for the early payment discount

operands.name: payment date
operands.constraints: used by the eligibility test and by the overdue test

operands.name: next payment date boundary
operands.constraints: an instalment maturing on or before it takes the kind that marks it as falling before the boundary

operands.name: direction sign
operands.constraints: the unsigned residuals are the residuals multiplied by its negation

preconditions.condition: The document has payment term lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The list is empty and the portal shows the document residual alone.

procedure: Sort the payment term lines by maturity date, a missing maturity date sorting last, and then by accounting date.
Walk them, numbering from one.

Record for each line its number, the line itself, the maturity date or the accounting date when there is none, the residual and the residual in currency, their unsigned counterparts obtained by multiplying the residuals by the negation of the direction sign, a kind, and whether the line is reconciled.
Give a reconciled line the kind that means no particular state and skip it for the rest of the walk.

When the document is still eligible for the early payment discount at the given payment currency and payment date, give the line the early-discount kind, replace its amounts by the stored discounted amounts, record the difference between the full and the discounted amount as the discount, and move on.
Otherwise decide the kind of the line by the kind rules.
records.formula: unsigned residual = residual × ( − direction sign ) ; discount recorded on an early-discount instalment = full amount − discounted amount

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the residuals and the stored discounted amounts are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the residual, the document currency for the residual in currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the instalment list
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it is displayed in the portal and consumed by the routine that derives the next payment values.

edge_cases.outcome: It sorts last and its accounting date is recorded in place of the maturity date.

edge_cases.case: A payment term line is already reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: It keeps the neutral kind and is skipped for the rest of the walk, so it can never become the overdue or the next instalment.

edge_cases.case: The document is eligible for the early payment discount.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalment carries the discounted amounts instead of the full ones and records the discount.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is minus one, so the unsigned residual is the residual itself, which is positive.

records.name: Deciding the kind of an instalment
records.purpose: Labels each unreconciled instalment as falling before a boundary, overdue, or next, which is what the portal uses to decide what to ask the customer to pay.

operands.name: maturity date of the instalment
operands.constraints: compared with the boundary and with the payment date

operands.name: next payment date boundary
operands.constraints: when given, an instalment maturing on or before it takes the boundary kind

operands.name: payment date
operands.constraints: an instalment maturing strictly before it is overdue

operands.name: first mode set during the walk
operands.constraints: the first overdue instalment sets the mode, and so does the first instalment that is neither overdue nor bounded

preconditions.condition: The instalment is not reconciled and not eligible for the early payment discount.
preconditions.otherwise: It carries the neutral kind or the early-discount kind and these rules do not apply.

procedure: Give the instalment the boundary kind when a next payment date boundary was given and the maturity date falls on or before it.
Otherwise give it the overdue kind when the maturity date falls strictly before the payment date, and let this also become the first mode.
Otherwise give it the next kind when no first mode has been set yet, and let this become the first mode.
Otherwise give it the next kind when the current mode is the overdue one, so that the first instalment after the overdue block is marked as the next one.
records.formula: kind = the boundary kind when a boundary was given and maturity date ≤ boundary ; else the overdue kind when maturity date < payment date, which also sets the first mode ; else the next kind when no first mode has been set, which sets the first mode ; else the next kind when the current mode is the overdue one

rounding.what: Nothing; the comparisons are on whole calendar dates.
rounding.precision: One day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the kind of each instalment
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; read by the routine that derives the next payment values and shown in the portal.

edge_cases.case: The maturity date equals the payment date.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalment is not overdue, since the test is a strict comparison.

edge_cases.case: Several instalments are overdue.
edge_cases.outcome: All of them carry the overdue kind, and the first instalment after them carries the next kind.

edge_cases.case: A boundary is given and every instalment matures after it.
edge_cases.outcome: No instalment carries the boundary kind and the ordinary rules apply.

worked_examples.description: Three instalments due the tenth of January, the tenth of February and the tenth of March of the year 2026, none reconciled, on a payment date of the first of February.

expected_outputs.kind of the third instalment: no kind assigned by these rules

worked_examples.narrative: The first instalment matured before the payment date, so it is overdue and sets the mode; the second is the first after the overdue block, so it is the next one; the third falls after it and takes no further kind.

worked_examples.description: The same three instalments with a boundary of the twenty-eighth of February.
worked_examples.narrative: The first two mature on or before the boundary and take the boundary kind, and the third is the first to fall outside it.

records.name: The next payment values when some instalments are overdue
records.purpose: Tells the portal what to collect when the customer is late, namely the whole overdue block rather than a single instalment.

operands.name: unsigned residuals of the overdue instalments
operands.constraints: summed

operands.name: document residual
operands.constraints: shown as the amount due

operands.name: document number
operands.constraints: the reference is that number, a hyphen and the first overdue instalment's number

operands.name: maturity date of the first overdue instalment
operands.constraints: shown as the next due date

preconditions.condition: There is more than one instalment, so instalments are shown at all.
preconditions.otherwise: The branch that shows no instalment applies and the whole document residual is asked for.

preconditions.condition: At least one instalment is overdue.
preconditions.otherwise: The branch for the next unreconciled instalment applies.

procedure: Set the instalment state to the overdue state.
Set the amount due to the document residual.
Set the next amount to pay to the sum of the unsigned residuals of all overdue instalments.
Set the next reference to the document number, a hyphen and the first overdue instalment's number.
Set the next due date to the first overdue instalment's maturity date.
records.formula: state = overdue ; amount due = the document residual ; next amount to pay = Σ over the overdue instalments of ( unsigned residual ) ; next reference = the document number + a hyphen + the first overdue instalment's number ; next due date = the first overdue instalment's maturity date

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the residuals are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the next payment values
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the portal and used to preset the amount of a payment.

edge_cases.case: Several instalments are overdue.
edge_cases.outcome: The next amount to pay is their sum, so the customer settles the whole overdue block at once.

edge_cases.case: The document residual exceeds the overdue block.

records.name: The next payment values when an unreconciled instalment remains
records.purpose: Tells the portal what to collect when nothing is overdue but instalments remain, namely the next one alone.

operands.name: unsigned residual of the first unreconciled instalment
operands.constraints: the amount asked for

operands.name: document residual
operands.constraints: shown as the amount due

operands.name: document number and instalment number
operands.source: the document and the instalment list
operands.constraints: joined by a hyphen to form the reference

operands.name: maturity date of that instalment
operands.constraints: shown as the next due date

preconditions.condition: There is more than one instalment, so instalments are shown at all.
preconditions.otherwise: The branch that shows no instalment applies.

preconditions.condition: No instalment is overdue and at least one remains unreconciled.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other three branches applies.

procedure: Set the instalment state to the next state.

Set the next amount to pay to the first unreconciled instalment's unsigned residual.
Set the next reference to the document number, a hyphen and that instalment's number.

records.formula: state = next ; amount due = the document residual ; next amount to pay = the unsigned residual of the first unreconciled instalment ; next reference = the document number + a hyphen + that instalment's number ; next due date = that instalment's maturity date

rounding.what: Nothing at this step.

rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the next payment values

edge_cases.case: The first instalment is already reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: The next unreconciled one is taken, and its own number appears in the reference.

edge_cases.case: Only one instalment remains unreconciled out of several.

worked_examples.description: A document of two instalments whose first has been paid, the second of 847.00 falling due the sixth of March of the year 2026.

operands.name: unsigned residual of the early-discount instalment

operands.constraints: shown as the amount due

operands.name: document residual
operands.constraints: shown as the next amount to pay, that is the full amount

operands.name: document number
operands.constraints: the reference is the plain document number, with no instalment number

operands.name: maturity date of that instalment
operands.constraints: shown as the next due date

preconditions.condition: The instalment list carries an instalment of the early-discount kind.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other three branches applies.

procedure: Set the instalment state to the early-discount state.
Set the amount due to that instalment's unsigned residual, which is the discounted amount.
Set the next amount to pay to the document residual, which is the full amount.
Set the next reference to the plain document number.
Set the next due date to that instalment's maturity date.
Produce the three extra values: the days left, the discount amount and the message.
records.formula: state = early payment discount ; amount due = the unsigned residual of the early-discount instalment, that is the discounted amount ; next amount to pay = the document residual, that is the full amount ; next reference = the document number ; next due date = that instalment's maturity date

rounding.what: Nothing at this step.
rounding.precision: The document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the next payment values in the discount case

edge_cases.case: The document has several instalments and the first is eligible.
edge_cases.outcome: The reference is still the plain document number, without an instalment number.

edge_cases.case: The customer supplies an amount that is neither the discounted amount nor the full one.
edge_cases.outcome: The branch for a custom amount takes over and the state is forced to the next state.

worked_examples.description: An invoice of 1 210.00 whose stored discounted amount is 1 185.80, still within the deadline.

records.name: The next payment values when no instalment is shown

operands.name: document number
operands.constraints: the reference is the plain number

operands.name: due date of the document
operands.constraints: shown as the next due date

preconditions.condition: None of the three earlier branches applies, that is there is no overdue instalment, no remaining unreconciled instalment to single out and no early-discount instalment.
preconditions.otherwise: That branch applies instead.

procedure: Set the instalment state to none.
Set the amount due to the document residual.
Set the next amount to pay to the document residual.
Set the next reference to the plain document number.
Set the next due date to the document's due date.
records.formula: state = none ; amount due = the document residual ; next amount to pay = the document residual ; next reference = the document number ; next due date = the document's due date

rounding.what: Nothing at this step.
rounding.precision: The document currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the next payment values
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the portal and used to preset the amount of a payment.

edge_cases.case: The document has a single instalment.
edge_cases.outcome: Instalments are not shown, so this branch applies and the reference carries no instalment number.

edge_cases.case: The document is fully paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual is zero and the portal asks for nothing.

worked_examples.description: A partly paid invoice with a single instalment and a residual of 1 182.76.

records.name: The days left before the discount deadline and the discount message
records.purpose: Tells the customer how long the discount stands and by how much it would reduce the payment, in the exact words the portal shows.

operands.name: discount deadline
operands.constraints: the date up to which the discount applies

operands.name: today
operands.constraints: subtracted from the deadline

operands.name: discount amount
operands.source: the difference between the full amount and the discounted amount recorded on the instalment
operands.constraints: formatted in the document currency inside the message

preconditions.condition: The instalment list carries an instalment of the early-discount kind.
preconditions.otherwise: Neither the days left nor the message is produced.

procedure: Subtract today from the discount deadline to obtain the number of days left, taking zero when the difference would be negative.
When at least one day remains, show the message that names the discount amount formatted in the document currency and the number of days left.
When no day remains, show the message that names the discount amount formatted in the document currency and says the payment must be made today.
records.formula: days_left = max( 0 , discount_date − today ) ; the message reads: Discount of *the discount amount formatted in the document currency* if paid within *days_left* days ; or, when no day remains: Discount of *the discount amount formatted in the document currency* if paid today

rounding.what: The number of days is a whole number of days; the amount is formatted at the precision of the document currency.
rounding.precision: One day, and the number of decimal places of the document currency.
rounding.method: The subtraction gives whole days and the negative case is clamped to zero.
rounding.step: The clamping after the subtraction, and the formatting when the message is built.

result.name: the days left and the discount message
result.unit_or_currency: whole days and the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the portal beside the discounted amount.

edge_cases.case: Today equals the deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: No day remains and the message that says the payment must be made today is shown.

edge_cases.case: Today is after the deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The days left are clamped to zero; the eligibility test would ordinarily have removed the early-discount kind in that case.

edge_cases.case: Several days remain.
edge_cases.outcome: The message names that number of days.

worked_examples.description: A deadline of the thirtieth of January of the year 2026, seen on the twenty-fifth of January.

expected_outputs.message: Discount of 24.20 in the document currency if paid within 5 days

worked_examples.narrative: Five days remain, so the portal offers the discount of 24.20 for five more days.

worked_examples.description: The same deadline seen on the thirtieth of January.

expected_outputs.message: Discount of 24.20 in the document currency if paid today

worked_examples.narrative: No day remains, so the message that names today is shown.

records.name: The next payment values when the caller supplies a custom amount
records.purpose: Lets a customer pay a figure of their own choosing, by overriding the amount, the reference and the due date the portal would otherwise offer.

operands.name: custom amount
operands.constraints: the override applies only when it is neither the next amount to pay nor, in the discount case, the discounted amount due

operands.name: next amount to pay computed by the ordinary branches
operands.constraints: compared with the custom amount

operands.name: discounted amount due
operands.constraints: also compared with the custom amount

operands.name: maturity date of the first instalment
operands.constraints: becomes the next due date

preconditions.condition: A custom amount is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary branch stands.

preconditions.condition: The custom amount differs from the next amount to pay and, in the discount case, from the discounted amount due.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary branch stands, since the customer chose exactly what was offered.

procedure: Compare the custom amount with the next amount to pay and, in the discount case, with the discounted amount due.
Force the instalment state to the next state.
Set the next amount to the custom amount.
Set the next reference to the plain document number.
Set the next due date to the first instalment's maturity date.
records.formula: custom amount ≠ next amount to pay and, in the discount case, ≠ the discounted amount due → state = next , next amount = the custom amount , next reference = the document number , next due date = the first instalment's maturity date

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the custom amount is taken as supplied.
rounding.precision: The document currency.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the overridden next payment values
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed in the portal and used to preset the payment.

edge_cases.case: The custom amount equals the next amount to pay.
edge_cases.outcome: No override happens and the ordinary branch stands, instalment number included in the reference.

edge_cases.case: The custom amount equals the discounted amount due in the discount case.
edge_cases.outcome: No override happens and the discount branch stands.

edge_cases.case: The custom amount exceeds the document residual.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still taken, and the payment leaves the document overpaid.

worked_examples.description: A customer choosing to pay one thousand against an invoice whose next amount to pay is 2 182.76.

records.name: The remaining values of the portal payment computation
records.purpose: Lists the further figures the portal receives beside the next payment values, so that the customer sees what has been paid and what remains.

operands.name: payment status of the document
operands.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a stored selection value
operands.constraints: carried through unchanged

operands.name: gross total of the document
operands.constraints: the residual is subtracted from it

operands.name: document residual
operands.constraints: subtracted from the total to give the amount already paid

operands.name: due date of the document
operands.constraints: carried through

operands.name: instalment list
operands.source: the walk over the payment term lines
operands.constraints: the unreconciled instalments are listed

preconditions.condition: The totals of the document are current.
preconditions.otherwise: The amount already paid does not match the reconciliations.

Carry through the document's due date.
List the unreconciled instalments.

result.name: the complete portal result

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual equals the total and the amount already paid is zero.

edge_cases.case: One instalment remains out of several.
edge_cases.outcome: The result says so, which lets the portal offer the whole remaining balance.

edge_cases.case: The document is fully paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The residual is zero and the amount already paid equals the gross total.
