records.name: Worked example of a partial payment against an invoice
records.purpose: Carries one partial settlement from the reconciliation to the new residual, the new payment status and the figures the portal then shows.

operands.name: invoice
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency, which is also the company currency
operands.source: the three-line invoice with two taxes
operands.constraints: a gross total of 2 182.76, a single instalment due the fifteenth of March of the year 2026

operands.name: payment
operands.source: a bank transfer registered on the twentieth of March of the year 2026
operands.constraints: one thousand

operands.name: payment reference
operands.constraints: the document number

preconditions.condition: The invoice is posted and its receivable line carries a residual.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to reconcile.

preconditions.condition: The payment is reconciled against the invoice's receivable line.
preconditions.otherwise: The invoice's residual does not move.

procedure: Record the state before the payment: a receivable line balance and residual of plus 2 182.76, a document residual of 2 182.76 and a payment status meaning not paid.
Create a partial reconciliation of 1 000.00 between the payment's receivable line, a credit of 1 000.00, and the invoice's receivable line, a debit of 2 182.76.
Compute the new residual of the receivable line as 2 182.76 less 1 000.00, rounded to the company currency.
Derive the document residual as the negation of the direction sign times the residual in currency.
Read the new payment status as partly paid, because the residual is not zero and a reconciliation row exists.
Note that the payment produces its own entry and that no journal item is added to the invoice.
records.formula: receivable_residual = round( 2182.76 − 1000.00 , company_currency ) = 1182.76 ; receivable_residual_currency = 1182.76 ; amount_residual = −( −1 ) × 1182.76 = 1182.76 ; amount already paid = 2182.76 − 1182.76 = 1000.00

rounding.what: The new residual of the receivable line.
rounding.precision: The company currency.
rounding.step: After the subtraction of the reconciled amount.

result.name: the state of the invoice after the partial payment
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency, which is also the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: The residual is stored on the receivable line, the payment status on the document, and the portal figures are computed from them.

edge_cases.case: The remaining 1 182.76 is paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The receivable line's residual reaches zero, its reconciled flag becomes true, a full reconciliation record is created and the payment status becomes paid, or the status meaning in payment when the company distinguishes the two and the payments are not yet matched with a bank statement.

edge_cases.case: The invoice has a single instalment.
edge_cases.outcome: The next reference is the plain document number with no hyphenated instalment number.

edge_cases.case: The payment's own entry is examined.
edge_cases.outcome: It carries a debit of 1 000.00 on the outstanding receipts account and a credit of 1 000.00 on the customer account; no journal item is added to the invoice.

worked_examples.description: The invoice before and after the payment.
worked_examples.narrative: A partial reconciliation of 1 000.00 leaves a residual of 1 182.76 on the receivable line, so the line is not reconciled, the document residual is 1 182.76, the status reads as partly paid, and the portal shows 1 000.00 already paid and 1 182.76 still to pay under the plain document number.

records.name: Worked example of a credit note issued against a paid invoice
records.purpose: Carries the reversal of one line of a settled invoice from the wizard to the credit note's entry and to the two ways of settling it, so that a rebuild reproduces the amounts, the header and the effect on the original invoice.

operands.name: original invoice
operands.source: the three-line invoice with two taxes
operands.constraints: a gross total of 2 182.76, fully paid on the twentieth of March of the year 2026

operands.name: reversal date
operands.constraints: the second of April of the year 2026

operands.name: reason
operands.constraints: carried into the reference of the credit note

operands.name: line kept on the credit note
operands.source: the user's edit of the copied lines
operands.constraints: forty printed manuals at 14.50 with a discount of ten per cent, taxed at twenty-one per cent

preconditions.condition: The source is an invoice and the plain reversal is used.
preconditions.otherwise: The cancelling reversal automatically reconciles the two documents, which applies to plain journal entries and to the mode that reverses and creates a new invoice.

preconditions.condition: The original invoice is fully paid.
preconditions.otherwise: The credit note may be reconciled against it and the invoice's residual and status change.

procedure: Open the reversal wizard on the invoice with the reversal date and the reason, and use the plain reversal, so the credit note is created as a draft that is not automatically reconciled.
Let the credit note copy every line, then delete the lines that are not being credited, leaving the second line.

Fill the header: the type is a customer credit note, it records that it reverses the invoice, its reference names the reversal and the reason, its accounting date, document date and due date are the reversal date, its journal is the invoice's journal, its payment term is cleared unless the invoice's term used the early-discount mode that books the discount on the invoice, its salesperson and origin are copied, its automatic posting is set to the value meaning at the date when the reversal date is in the future and to the value meaning none otherwise, and its recipient bank account is cleared and recomputed.
Compute the amounts of the single remaining line: a net amount of forty times 14.50 times ninety hundredths and a tax of twenty-one per cent on it.
Build the journal items with a direction sign of plus one, so the product line is a debit and the receivable line a credit.
Post the credit note, which takes a number from the credit-note sequence when the journal has a dedicated one and from the ordinary sequence otherwise.
Settle it either by registering an outbound payment of the gross amount, or by leaving it unreconciled as an open credit.

rounding.what: The net amount of the line and its tax.
rounding.precision: Two decimal places.
rounding.step: The net amount first, then the tax on the rounded net amount.

result.name: the credit note and its settlement
result.stored_or_displayed: Three journal items on the credit note, its own number, and either a payment entry or an open credit on the customer's account.

edge_cases.case: The invoice's payment term used the early-discount mode that books the discount on the invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: The payment term is kept on the credit note rather than cleared.

edge_cases.case: The reversal date is in the future.
edge_cases.outcome: The automatic posting of the credit note is set to the value meaning at the date.

edge_cases.case: The credit note is left unreconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: It appears in the outstanding credits block of every future invoice of that customer and lowers the customer's receivable aggregate by its gross amount.

edge_cases.case: The invoice had been unpaid and the credit note is reconciled against it.
edge_cases.outcome: The invoice's residual drops by the credit note's gross amount and its payment status becomes partly paid; had the credit note covered the whole invoice, the status would have become the one meaning reversed rather than paid, since the residual is zero, there is no payment counterpart and the only counterpart type is a customer credit note.

worked_examples.description: The credit note for the second line of the invoice.
worked_examples.narrative: The single line credits nothing and debits 522.00 of revenue and 109.62 of tax, against a credit of 631.62 on the receivable account; the invoice is already paid, so the credit note's residual stays 631.62 and the invoice is untouched.

worked_examples.description: Refunding the customer.
worked_examples.narrative: The outbound payment debits the customer account and credits the outstanding payments account, and reconciling it with the credit note's receivable line brings the residual to zero.

records.name: The currency rate stored on a document
records.purpose: Fixes the rate at which a foreign-currency document is translated into the company currency, and freezes it on the document so that a later change of the rate table cannot silently restate a posted document.

operands.name: company currency
operands.source: the company that owns the document
operands.constraints: the source of the conversion

operands.name: document currency
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

operands.name: rate date
operands.source: the document date, or today when there is none
operands.constraints: the date at which the rate table is read

operands.name: override typed by the user
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive; it survives until the currency, the company, the document date or the taxable supply date changes

preconditions.condition: The rate is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused with the message “The currency rate must be strictly positive.”

preconditions.condition: The document is an invoice and its currency differs from the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The constraint on the rate does not apply and the rate is one.

procedure: Take the rate date as the document date, or today when the document has none.
Read the conversion rate from the company currency to the document currency, for the company, at that date.
Store that rate on the document as a value of its own, not as a lookup, so that a later change of the rate table leaves a posted document untouched.
Let the user override it, and keep the override until the currency, the company, the document date or the taxable supply date changes, at which point the expected rate is read again.
records.formula: expected_rate = conversion_rate( company_currency → document_currency , company , rate_date )   with   rate_date = invoice_date , or today when there is none

rounding.what: Nothing; the rate is stored as read from the rate table or as typed.
rounding.precision: The precision the rate table carries.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the currency rate of the document
result.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and applied to every line's conversion.

edge_cases.case: The rate is set to zero or to a negative value.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused with the message “The currency rate must be strictly positive.”

edge_cases.case: The document has no document date.
edge_cases.outcome: Today is used as the rate date.

edge_cases.case: The rate table changes after the document is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The document keeps the rate it stored, so its company-currency amounts do not move.

edge_cases.case: The user changes the document date after overriding the rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The override is dropped and the expected rate is read again at the new date.

worked_examples.description: An invoice in a foreign currency issued on the fourth of May of the year 2026, where one unit of the company currency buys 1.0850 units of the document currency.
worked_examples.narrative: The rate table is read at the document date and the value is stored on the document, where it stays even if the table changes later.

records.name: The rate of a line and the conversion between its two amounts
records.purpose: States which rate each line uses and how a line's balance and its amount in currency are derived from one another, so that the two currency columns of an entry always agree.

operands.name: rate of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the line currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the document's rate on an invoice, and a per-line lookup at the document date on a document that is not an invoice
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: amount in currency of the line
operands.constraints: accounting-signed

operands.name: balance of the line
operands.constraints: accounting-signed, of the same sign as the amount in currency

preconditions.condition: The line has a currency and a rate.
preconditions.otherwise: No conversion can be performed.

preconditions.condition: The document is an invoice.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is looked up per line at the document date rather than taken from the document.

procedure: Take the document's rate for every line of an invoice, and look the rate up per line at the document date on a document that is not an invoice.
Derive a line's balance from its amount in currency by dividing by the rate and rounding to the company currency.
Derive a line's amount in currency from its balance by multiplying by the rate and rounding to the line currency.
records.formula: balance = round( amount_currency ÷ rate , company_currency )   and   amount_currency = round( balance × rate , line_currency )

rounding.what: The derived amount.
rounding.precision: The company currency in the first direction, the line currency in the second.
rounding.step: Once, after the division or the multiplication, before the amount is stored.

result.name: the two amounts of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the line currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the journal item as its amount in currency and its balance.

edge_cases.case: The line currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one and the two amounts are equal, as the stored-value check on the sign requires.

edge_cases.case: The document is a plain journal entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Each line's rate is looked up separately at the document date, so two lines in different currencies may carry different rates.

edge_cases.case: A cost-of-goods-sold line is examined.
edge_cases.outcome: It is always in the company currency, unlike every other line of an invoice, which carries the document currency.

worked_examples.description: A product line of one thousand in the document currency on an invoice whose rate is 1.0850.
worked_examples.narrative: The amount in currency divided by the rate is minus 921.658986 and more, which rounds to minus 921.66 in the company currency.

worked_examples.description: A balance of minus 921.66 converted back at the same rate.
worked_examples.narrative: The balance times the rate is minus 999.9999, which rounds back to minus 1 000.00 in the line currency.

records.name: The three places where a rate other than the document rate is used
records.purpose: Names the exceptions to the rule that every conversion on an invoice uses the document's stored rate, so that a rebuild does not apply that rate where another one governs.

operands.name: effective rate of the payment term distribution
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the absolute value of the ratio of the total in the document currency to the total in the company currency
operands.constraints: derived from the totals, not read from the document

operands.name: rate table reading for the cash rounding line
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the currency rate table at the document date, or the accounting date when there is none
operands.constraints: read for the company

operands.name: new rate after an edit
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the document, after the user changed it
operands.constraints: applied only to the balances of the tax lines

preconditions.condition: The document is a foreign-currency document.
preconditions.otherwise: Every rate is one and the exceptions make no observable difference.

procedure: Use the effective rate of the distribution, the absolute value of the ratio of the two totals, for the payment term instalments, so that they add up in both currencies.
Convert the cash rounding line's balance from the document currency at the document date, or the accounting date when there is none, using the currency rate table and not the document's stored rate.

Under the rounding source that reapplies the currency rate, recompute each tax line's balance as its amount in currency divided by the new rate, rounded to the company currency, preserving the amount in currency.
records.formula: payment term distribution : rate = | total_in_currency ÷ total_company | ; cash rounding line : balance = convert( difference , document currency → company currency , company , document date or accounting date ) from the rate table ; tax line under the reapplied rate : balance = round( amount_currency ÷ new_rate , company_currency )

rounding.what: Each converted amount.
rounding.precision: The company currency.
rounding.step: Once per conversion, after the division or the table lookup.

result.name: the converted amounts under the three exceptions
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the balances of the payment term lines, of the cash rounding line and of the tax lines.

edge_cases.case: The effective rate differs from the document's stored rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The instalments follow the effective rate, which is what makes them add up exactly to the company-currency total of the document.

edge_cases.case: The document has no document date.
edge_cases.outcome: The cash rounding line's conversion uses the accounting date.

edge_cases.case: The rate is edited on a document whose tax lines already exist.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the balances of the tax lines are recomputed; their amounts in currency are preserved.

worked_examples.description: A foreign-currency invoice of 1 210.00 in the document currency worth 1 115.21 in the company currency, whose stored rate is 1.0850.
worked_examples.narrative: The instalment is the last line of its term, so it takes the residual in both currencies and the two columns match exactly; dividing 1 210.00 by the stored rate would give 1 115.2074 and more, which happens to round to the same figure here, but the balance rule guarantees the match even where the two would differ.

worked_examples.description: A tax line of minus 210.00 in the document currency after the rate is changed to 1.1000.
worked_examples.narrative: The amount in currency is preserved and only the balance is recomputed from the new rate.

records.name: Worked example of a foreign-currency invoice from the lines to the totals
records.purpose: Carries one invoice in a currency other than the company's from the amounts in the document currency to the two-column entry and the eight total fields, so that a rebuild can check both currency columns against a known result.

operands.name: product line
operands.constraints: four units at 250.00, no discount, taxed at twenty-one per cent

operands.name: currency rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.source: the rate table at the document date

operands.name: payment term
operands.constraints: a single line of one hundred per cent at thirty days

operands.name: document date
operands.constraints: the fourth of May of the year 2026

preconditions.condition: The rate is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The write is refused.

preconditions.condition: The document currency differs from the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The two columns coincide.

procedure: Compute the amounts in the document currency: a net of four times 250.00 and a tax of twenty-one per cent on it.
Convert each to the company currency by dividing by the rate and rounding.
Apply the payment term: the single line is the last one, so the balance rule gives it the whole residual in both currencies.
Build the three journal items in accounting signs, with a direction sign of minus one.
Fill the totals in each currency.
records.formula: net_currency = round( 4 × 250.00 , document currency ) = 1000.00 ; tax_currency = round( 1000.00 × 0.21 , document currency ) = 210.00 ; gross_currency = 1210.00 ; net_balance = round( 1000.00 ÷ 1.0850 , company currency ) = round( 921.658986… ) = 921.66 ; tax_balance = round( 210.00 ÷ 1.0850 , company currency ) = round( 193.548387… ) = 193.55 ; gross_balance = 921.66 + 193.55 = 1115.21

rounding.what: Each amount in the document currency and each converted balance.
rounding.precision: The document currency for the first, the company currency for the second.
rounding.step: The document-currency amounts first, then each conversion; the receivable line takes the residual in both currencies and is not rounded again.

result.name: the foreign-currency invoice and its totals
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Three journal items carrying both columns, and the eight total fields of the document.

edge_cases.case: The receivable line's company-currency amount is compared with the direct conversion.
edge_cases.outcome: Dividing 1 210.00 by 1.0850 gives 1 115.2074 and more, which rounds to 1 115.21 as well; the balance rule guarantees the match even where the two would differ.

edge_cases.case: Both columns are summed.
edge_cases.outcome: The company-currency column balances at zero and so does the document-currency column.

worked_examples.description: The complete invoice.

inputs.payment term: one line of 100 per cent at 30 days

expected_outputs.product line: a credit of 921.66 in the company currency and minus 1 000.00 in the document currency
expected_outputs.tax line: a credit of 193.55 in the company currency and minus 210.00 in the document currency
expected_outputs.receivable line: a debit of 1 115.21 in the company currency and plus 1 210.00 in the document currency

worked_examples.narrative: The customer reads 1 000.00 net, 210.00 of tax and 1 210.00 in total in the document currency, while the ledger carries 921.66, 193.55 and 1 115.21 in the company currency; both columns balance.

records.name: The exchange difference when a foreign-currency receivable is settled at another rate
records.purpose: Measures the company-currency difference that remains when a payment clears the document-currency residual exactly, and books it so that both residuals reach zero.

operands.name: company-currency value of the receivable line
operands.constraints: computed at the document's rate

operands.name: company-currency value of the payment
operands.source: the payment, computed at the rate of the payment date
operands.constraints: differs from the first when the rate moved

operands.name: reconciliation date
operands.constraints: the date of the exchange difference entry

preconditions.condition: The payment clears the document-currency residual exactly.
preconditions.otherwise: A residual remains in the document currency too and the document is only partly settled.

preconditions.condition: The company-currency amounts differ.
preconditions.otherwise: No exchange difference entry is created.

procedure: Convert the payment at the rate of its own date to obtain its company-currency value.
Subtract that value from the company-currency value of the receivable line to obtain the exchange difference.
Create an exchange difference entry in the exchange journal, dated at the reconciliation date.
Book the difference to the exchange loss account when the correcting amount is positive and to the exchange gain account otherwise, against the same receivable account.
Reconcile the counterpart line with the invoice's receivable line so that both residuals reach zero, and set the payment status to paid.
records.formula: exchange_difference = 1115.21 − 1100.00 = 15.21

rounding.what: The company-currency value of the payment.
rounding.precision: The company currency.
rounding.step: When the payment is converted, before the subtraction; the difference itself is not rounded again.

result.name: the exchange difference and its entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a separate journal entry in the exchange journal, whose counterpart is reconciled with the invoice's receivable line.

edge_cases.case: The rate moved against the company.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is positive and lands on the exchange loss account.

edge_cases.case: The rate moved in favour of the company.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is negative and lands on the exchange gain account.

edge_cases.case: The reconciliation is undone.
edge_cases.outcome: The exchange difference entry is reversed.

worked_examples.description: A payment of 1 210.00 in the document currency on the tenth of June of the year 2026, when one unit of the company currency buys 1.1000 units of the document currency, against an invoice booked at 1 115.21.
worked_examples.narrative: The payment is worth 1 100.00 in the company currency against a receivable of 1 115.21, so an exchange difference entry books a loss of 15.21 and credits the customer account by the same amount; reconciling that counterpart brings both residuals to zero.

records.name: The effect of editing the currency rate after the lines exist
records.purpose: States which amounts move and which stay when a user changes a document's rate on a draft that already carries product lines, tax lines and payment term lines.

operands.name: new currency rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the document currency for one unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: amounts in currency of the tax lines
operands.constraints: preserved across the edit

operands.name: unit prices and quantities of the product lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency and the unit of measure
operands.constraints: the product line amounts are recomputed from them as usual

preconditions.condition: Only the currency rate changed.
preconditions.otherwise: An earlier condition of the rounding source cascade matches and the tax amounts are recomputed from the bases instead.

preconditions.condition: The document status is draft.
preconditions.otherwise: The synchronisation does not run.

procedure: Set the tax synchronisation's rounding source to the one that reapplies the currency rate.
Preserve the amounts in currency of the tax lines and recompute only their balances as the amount in currency divided by the new rate, rounded to the company currency.
Recompute the product line amounts from the unit price, the quantity and the discount as usual.
Rebuild the payment term lines from the new totals, since they are reconciled last.
records.formula: tax line : balance = round( amount_currency ÷ new_rate , company_currency ), the amount in currency preserved ; product lines recomputed from the unit price ; payment term lines rebuilt from the new totals

rounding.what: Each recomputed balance.
rounding.precision: The company currency.
rounding.step: After the division by the new rate, once per line.

result.name: the restated company-currency column
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the balances of the tax lines, the product lines and the payment term lines.

edge_cases.case: The document is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate cannot be changed through the synchronisation, because a posted document is never synchronised.

edge_cases.case: The currency itself is changed rather than the rate.
edge_cases.outcome: The first condition of the rounding source cascade matches and every tax amount is recomputed from the bases.

edge_cases.case: The new rate is not strictly positive.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused with the message “The currency rate must be strictly positive.”

worked_examples.description: The foreign-currency invoice whose rate is changed from 1.0850 to 1.1000.
worked_examples.narrative: The tax line keeps its 210.00 in the document currency and its balance becomes minus 190.91; the product line is recomputed from the unit price, giving a balance of minus 909.09, and the payment term line is rebuilt last from the new totals, taking 1 210.00 in the document currency and 1 100.00 in the company currency.

records.name: The gross total spelled out in words
records.purpose: Produces the written form of the document total that some jurisdictions require on the printed document beside the figure.

operands.name: gross total of the document
operands.constraints: customer-facing and positive

operands.name: spelling rule of the document currency
operands.source: the currency, which carries its own names for the whole unit and the subdivision
operands.constraints: decides the exact wording

preconditions.condition: The document has a gross total and a currency.
preconditions.otherwise: No written form is produced.

procedure: Take the gross total of the document.
Spell it out in the document currency by that currency's own spelling rule, which names the whole units and the subdivision.
Remove every comma from the result.
records.formula: amount_total_words = the gross total spelled out in the document currency, with every comma removed

rounding.what: Nothing beyond the rounding the total already carries.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal places of the document currency, which fixes how many subdivision units are named.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the total was computed.
rounding.step: Not applicable to this step.

result.name: the total in words
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, a phrase naming an amount in the document currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the document and printed on it.

edge_cases.case: The total has no subdivision part.
edge_cases.outcome: The currency's spelling rule decides whether the subdivision is named at all.

edge_cases.case: The spelling rule produces commas.
edge_cases.outcome: Every comma is removed from the result.

edge_cases.case: The currency has no subdivision.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the whole units are named.

worked_examples.description: A total of 2 182.76 in a currency whose whole unit is the euro and whose subdivision is the cent.

expected_outputs.total in words: Two Thousand One Hundred Eighty-Two Euros and Seventy-Six Cents

worked_examples.narrative: The whole units and the subdivision are spelled by the currency's own rule and every comma is removed.

records.name: The rows of the payment term preview
records.purpose: Shows a user configuring a payment term what instalments it would produce on an example amount and an example date, before any document uses it.

operands.name: example amount
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency chosen for the preview
operands.constraints: used as the untaxed amount in both currencies

operands.name: example date
operands.constraints: used as the reference date

operands.name: tax total for the preview
operands.source: fixed at zero for the preview
operands.constraints: always zero

operands.name: sign parameter for the preview
operands.constraints: plus one

preconditions.condition: The payment term has at least one line.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to preview.

procedure: Run the payment term distribution with a tax total of zero, the example amount as the untaxed amount in both currencies, and a sign parameter of plus one.
Group the produced instalments by date.
Render one row per date, naming the row number, the instalment amount and the date it falls due.
records.formula: each row reads: N# Installment of *amount* due on *date* , one row per distinct maturity date produced by the distribution run with a tax total of zero and a sign parameter of plus one

rounding.what: Each instalment of the preview.
rounding.precision: The currency of the example amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, with the last line taking the residual under the balance rule.
rounding.step: Inside the distribution, exactly as for a real document.

result.name: the preview rows
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the example amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed beside the payment term while it is configured; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: Two lines of the term fall on the same date.
edge_cases.outcome: They are grouped into a single row, as they would merge into a single receivable line on a real document.

edge_cases.case: The term ends with a percent line whose percentages do not add up to one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The last row absorbs the difference under the balance rule, so the rows add up to the example amount.

edge_cases.case: The term carries an early discount.
edge_cases.outcome: An extra row is rendered above the instalment rows.

worked_examples.description: A term of thirty per cent immediately and seventy per cent at forty-five days, previewed on an example amount of one thousand and an example date of the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: With a tax total of zero the distribution cuts the example amount into 300.00 immediately and 700.00 at forty-five days, that is the sixth of March, and one row is rendered per date.

records.name: The early payment discount row of the payment term preview
records.purpose: Shows a user configuring a payment term what the customer would pay under the early payment discount, above the instalment rows.

operands.name: example amount
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency chosen for the preview
operands.constraints: the gross total handed to the printed-amount formula

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.constraints: divided by one hundred to give the discount ratio

operands.name: tax total for the preview
operands.source: fixed at zero for the preview
operands.constraints: makes both branches of the printed-amount formula coincide

operands.name: discount days
operands.constraints: added to the example date

preconditions.condition: The payment term carries an early discount.
preconditions.otherwise: No such row is rendered.

procedure: Compute the amount by the printed-amount formula with a tax total of zero, which makes both branches reduce to the example amount multiplied by one less the discount ratio, whatever the computation mode.
Add the discount days to the example date to obtain the date.
Format the date in the reader's language.
Render the row above the instalment rows, naming the amount and the date.
records.formula: amount = round( example_amount × ( 1 − p ) ) with p the discount percentage ÷ 100 ; date = example_date + discount_days ; the row reads: Early Payment Discount: *amount* if paid before *date*

rounding.what: The discounted amount.
rounding.precision: The currency of the example amount.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by one less the discount ratio.

result.name: the early payment discount row
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the example amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed above the instalment rows; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: The computation mode is one that discounts only the net part.
edge_cases.outcome: The preview still shows the whole-amount figure, because the tax total handed to the formula is zero and both branches then coincide.

edge_cases.case: The payment term carries no early discount.
edge_cases.outcome: No row is rendered.

edge_cases.case: A cash rounding method is configured on the document being previewed.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is corrected to a multiple of the coin.

worked_examples.description: A discount of two per cent within ten days previewed on an example amount of one thousand and an example date of the twentieth of January of the year 2026.
worked_examples.narrative: The example amount times 0.98 is 980.00, and ten days after the twentieth of January is the thirtieth, so the row offers 980.00 if paid before that date.

records.name: The abnormal amount and abnormal date warnings
records.purpose: Compares a document's total and date with the customer's usual pattern and warns when the deviation is large, without blocking the user.

operands.name: gross total of the document
operands.constraints: must be other than zero for the detection to run

operands.name: document date
operands.constraints: compared with the partner's usual interval

operands.name: history of the partner
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency and calendar dates
operands.source: the earlier documents of that partner
operands.constraints: must be long enough for a pattern to exist

operands.name: the two flags that silence the warnings
operands.source: the partner, as the indications to ignore an abnormal document date and to ignore an abnormal document amount
operands.constraints: when both are set the detection is skipped entirely

preconditions.condition: The document is a draft purchase document with a total other than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: Neither warning fires; they never fire on a customer invoice, where the two fields of the shared entity are always empty.

preconditions.condition: The partner does not carry both flags that silence the warnings, and the caller has not disabled abnormal detection.
preconditions.otherwise: The detection is skipped entirely.

procedure: Check that the document is a draft purchase document with a total other than zero.
Skip the detection when the partner carries both flags that silence the warnings, or when the caller disabled abnormal detection.
Compare the document's total with the customer's usual amount and its date with the customer's usual interval.
Show a warning banner when either deviation is large.
Leave the two corresponding fields empty on a receivable document, which is why neither warning is ever seen there.
records.formula: the detection runs only on a draft purchase document whose total ≠ 0 , and only when the partner does not carry both silencing flags ; on a receivable document both warning texts are always empty

rounding.what: Nothing; the comparison is on already-rounded totals and on whole calendar dates.
rounding.precision: The document currency and one day.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the two warning texts
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as two text fields of the document and displayed as warning banners in the alert list when they are not empty.

edge_cases.case: The document is a customer invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither warning fires and both fields stay empty; the two fields exist on the shared entity and their specification belongs to the payable documents.

edge_cases.case: The partner carries both silencing flags.
edge_cases.outcome: The detection is skipped entirely.

edge_cases.case: The total is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The detection does not run.

worked_examples.description: A draft customer invoice of 2 182.76 for a customer with a long history.
worked_examples.narrative: The detection runs on purchase documents only, so both fields stay empty and no banner appears on a receivable document.

records.name: The days-sales-outstanding of a customer
records.purpose: Expresses how long the customer takes to settle, as the share of the lifetime invoiced amount still outstanding applied to the age of the oldest document.

operands.name: receivable aggregate of the partner
operands.constraints: the amount still owed

operands.name: lifetime invoiced amount including tax
operands.source: the sum of the accounting-signed gross totals of every sale document of the active company for the partner's commercial entity, receipts included, excluding draft and cancelled documents
operands.constraints: the result is zero when this amount is zero and no division is performed

operands.name: days since the oldest document
operands.source: the number of whole days between the earliest document date of that same set and today
operands.constraints: zero when the set is empty, since the earliest date is then taken as today

preconditions.condition: The lifetime invoiced amount including tax is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero and no division is performed.

preconditions.condition: The set of sale documents is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The earliest date is taken as today and the number of days is zero.

procedure: Sum the accounting-signed gross totals, in the company currency, of every sale document of the active company for the partner's commercial entity, receipts included, excluding draft and cancelled documents.
Take the partner's receivable aggregate.
Count the whole days between the earliest document date of that set and today, taking the earliest date as today when the set is empty.
Divide the receivable aggregate by the lifetime invoiced amount and multiply by the number of days.
Report zero when the lifetime invoiced amount is zero, without performing the division.
records.formula: days_sales_outstanding = ( total_receivable ÷ total_invoiced_tax_included ) × days_since_oldest_invoice

rounding.what: The number of days is a whole number; the result is expressed with one decimal place in the worked example.
rounding.precision: One day for the age, and the display precision of the figure for the result.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the number of days.

result.name: days sales outstanding
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the partner in its receivable role.

edge_cases.case: The lifetime invoiced amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero and no division is performed.

edge_cases.case: The set of sale documents is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The earliest date is taken as today, so the number of days is zero and the result is zero.

edge_cases.case: The receivable aggregate exceeds the lifetime invoiced amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The ratio exceeds one and the figure exceeds the age of the oldest document, which signals an unusual account.

worked_examples.description: A customer with a receivable balance of twelve thousand, a lifetime invoiced amount of ninety thousand and an oldest document dated three hundred days ago.
worked_examples.narrative: Twelve thousand divided by ninety thousand is one hundred and thirty-three thousandths and more, and multiplied by three hundred days that gives forty days exactly.
